target: Cartograph Atlas — server-authoritative ECS column store + GPU-driven tiled compute rasterizer (re-architecture candidate for the Cartograph map mod on Satisfactory / CSS UE 5.3.2 fork, SML).

techniques.name: Native orthographic tiling on USceneCaptureComponent2D (enable_orthographic_tiling + num_x_tiles/num_y_tiles)
techniques.whatItIs: USceneCaptureComponent2D has a built-in mode that renders one orthographic capture split across NumXTiles x NumYTiles sub-captures over successive frames (ResetOrthographicTilingCounter resets the sequence). Each tile is an independent, bounded GPU submission into a sub-rect of the target. Works only in Orthographic projection with CaptureSource = SceneColor (not FinalColor).
techniques.appliesTo: renderPipeline (the candidate's whole 'fixed pyramid of 256x256 tiles, K dirty tiles/frame, hard per-frame primitive ceiling, TDR structurally impossible' goal); asyncThreading (frame-budgeted draining).
techniques.benefit: Delivers the candidate's #1 killer-feature (bounded per-frame GPU submission => no single pass can exceed the ~2s TDR window) as a stock engine feature with ZERO custom shaders, zero RDG, zero hand-rolled tile scheduler. A megabase capture drains over NumX*NumY frames automatically; each tile is a small submission. Eliminates the 'unbounded single GPU pass -> client crash #14' root cause without writing a rasterizer.
techniques.caveats: Requires CaptureSource=SceneColor (an unlit marker-mesh material gives clean color anyway); the candidate's pixel-perfect 256x256-atlas-tile scheme becomes 'engine ortho tiling across N frames', coarser (whole-view re-capture split across frames, not per-dirty-region) so it bounds GPU cost but does NOT alone give per-event dirty-tile locality. Pair with capture_every_frame=false + a debounced dirty flag and per-class instance components. Lowest-risk way to hit the TDR goal; the custom RDG rasterizer is only worth it if profiling shows ortho-tiling capture is too coarse.

techniques.name: Satisfactory's own AbstractInstance manager (AddInstance/RemoveInstance O(1), SetCustomPrimitiveDataOnHandle, ResolveHit)
techniques.whatItIs: In-repo plugin (Plugins/AbstractInstance) the game already uses for lightweight buildables. Exposes stable FInstanceOwnerHandlePtr identity, O(1) AddInstance/RemoveInstance (remove-swap with handle patch handled internally), per-class bucketed ULightweightHISM components, SetCustomPrimitiveDataOnHandle(s) for per-instance floats, and ResolveHit/ResolveOverlap for picking.
techniques.appliesTo: dataModel (stable generational handles -> a ready-made stable-handle instanced store); renderPipeline (per-class instance components feeding SceneCapture); asyncThreading (O(1) ingestion); serverClientPartitioning (client-side instance store).
techniques.benefit: Gives the candidate's 'stable handle, O(1) mutation, GPU-resident instance buffer, per-class table' for free, written by CSS, battle-tested at megabase scale on this exact game. The handle becomes the network/UI identity (replaces FBuildingHandle{slot,gen}); per-instance custom-data floats carry worldZ/layerId so a material clip() does Z-band + layer filtering on the GPU (replaces the separate Z-band index and the whole OnZFilterUpdated full-redraw). Removes the FBuildingData second copy, the redirector, and the quadtree at once.
techniques.caveats: ULightweightHISM here derives from UInstancedStaticMeshComponent (ShouldCreatePhysicsState=false) - the visual instancing path, fine for a marker layer. Build.cs must uncomment AbstractInstance in PublicDependencyModuleNames (currently disabled). Manager is World-scoped; the marker actor must live on a layer the main camera never renders (SceneCapture ShowOnlyActors). Per-instance custom-data uploads must be coalesced (MarkDirtyDeferred is provided). Strictly cheaper to adopt than hand-rolling a TSparseArray instance buffer + custom upload.

techniques.name: PerInstanceCustomData + material clip() for Z-band and layer filtering
techniques.whatItIs: InstancedStaticMeshComponent NumCustomDataFloats / SetCustomDataValue feed per-instance floats to a material's PerInstanceCustomData node with no extra draw calls. A material can clip()/discard fragments whose worldZ is outside MinZ/MaxZ scalar params or whose layer bit is masked.
techniques.appliesTo: dataModel (the candidate's coarse Z-band index / per-cell band bitmask); renderPipeline (Z/layer filter); asyncThreading (slider = set 2 scalars + 1 re-capture instead of O(N) re-walk).
techniques.benefit: Collapses the height-slider and layer-toggle paths from O(N) array re-walks (today's OnZFilterUpdated -> full redraw) to O(1) material-parameter sets + one debounced capture. Removes the candidate's separate Z-band index structure entirely - the Z value rides on the instance the engine already stores. Kills the 'operator<=> Z-sort coupling' the diagnosis flags as the root coupling, with no extra memory.
techniques.caveats: clip()-filtered instances still pay vertex + early-PS cost (culled in the pixel shader, not skipped on the vertex side). For extreme megabases, toggle whole per-class/per-layer component visibility for fully-disabled layers in addition to per-instance clip. Custom-data float count is fixed per component; budget channels (worldZ, layerId, categoryColorIndex) up front.

techniques.name: ReliableMessaging plugin: SendTaggedMessage over EOS/Steam/TCP, per-player components
techniques.whatItIs: In-repo CSS plugin (Plugins/ReliableMessaging, friendly name 'BulkDataReplication'). UReliableMessagingSubsystem::SendTaggedMessage(const APlayerController*, FGameplayTag, TArray<uint8>) sends a reliable large payload server<->client; chunking/acking/backpressure and lifetime are owned by the plugin and keyed on a per-player UReliableMessagingPlayerComponent, torn down on disconnect. Backends: EOS P2P, Steam P2P, TCP (server-capable).
techniques.appliesTo: networkTransport (the candidate's 'delta-by-tile-version, lazy AoI pull' channel); serverClientPartitioning (join transfer); fixes #9 by construction.
techniques.benefit: Exactly the transport the candidate specifies, already in-repo. Replaces the hand-rolled RCO that causes #9: no per-join synchronous Archive<<CurrentBuildingData on the game thread, no int16 slice overflow (plugin owns chunk widths), no unchecked TMap::Find() null-deref on a timeout race (plugin owns per-player lifetime), no move-unsafe FBufferWriter-in-a-TMap. Tag routing lets tile/AoI deltas and full-join streams coexist. Server-deny-list already set per backend.
techniques.caveats: Source-verified from the in-repo header, not external docs (private CSS plugin). SendTaggedMessage takes the payload BY VALUE (TArray<uint8>) so the caller still builds a per-message blob - keep tile blobs slim (~28B/record + RLE for empty tiles) and coalesce per net-tick. Tile versioning (uint32 = hash of authoritative content, not a session counter) and idempotent clear-then-apply per tile are the mod's responsibility; the plugin guarantees reliable delivery, not your delta semantics.

techniques.name: GPU Scene auto-instancing (SM5/SM6) on Satisfactory's Nanite-enabled fork
techniques.whatItIs: UE5's GPU Scene uploads instance transforms to a GPU-resident structured buffer and auto-instances identical static meshes into single instanced draws; with ISM/HISM, thousands of instances render in a handful of draws. Satisfactory ships Nanite (DX12/SM5+) so the SM5/SM6 GPU-driven path is active in the shipping game.
techniques.appliesTo: renderPipeline (the candidate's 'compact instance buffer via indirect/instanced draws'); memoryModel (the instance transform buffer IS the only count-scaling GPU buffer).
techniques.benefit: Confirms the candidate's premise that 'the map image is a GPU artifact computed from a compact instance buffer' is achievable with stock instanced rendering - no hand-written DrawIndexedInstancedIndirect or compute splat needed to get GPU-driven, draw-call-bounded rendering of the marker layer. One ISM/HISM per class + SceneCapture = the whole pipeline. Per-frame CPU drops to 'patch one instance + mark dirty', matching the candidate's O(1) target.
techniques.caveats: Nanite is irrelevant for a flat 2D marker quad (do NOT Nanite-enable the marker mesh - use a simple quad/unit-box). The win is auto-instancing + GPU Scene, on by default for ISM. Custom indirect-draw via RHIMultiDrawIndexedPrimitiveIndirect exists but is only justified for a single megabuffer of mixed geometry the ISM path can't express; for per-class quads/lines it is over-engineering vs AbstractInstance.

techniques.name: Custom global shaders / RDG compute from a plugin (FRDGBuilder via ENQUEUE_RENDER_COMMAND, Shaders dir, PostConfigInit module)
techniques.whatItIs: A plugin can ship HLSL global shaders by mapping a virtual /Plugin/Name path to its Shaders/ dir (AddShaderSourceDirectoryMapping via IPluginManager) and setting the shader-implementing module's LoadingPhase to PostConfigInit. RDG passes are buildable outside the renderer by constructing FRDGBuilder(RHICmdList) inside an ENQUEUE_RENDER_COMMAND lambda; dependencies are RenderCore + RHI (+ Projects for the dir mapping).
techniques.appliesTo: renderPipeline (the candidate's full custom GPU-driven tiled compute rasterizer / indirect-draw path and its RDG dispatches).
techniques.benefit: Makes the candidate's most aggressive variant (compute splat / DrawIndexedInstancedIndirect into per-tile scissored passes, hard primitive ceiling) genuinely possible from a mod without engine source changes - the path that would give true per-dirty-region (not whole-view) GPU locality and the tightest VRAM/bandwidth control.
techniques.caveats: Real friction on THIS mod: (1) the Cartograph module is LoadingPhase=Default and ships no Shaders dir - shaders need a separate PostConfigInit module (GameFeature plugins load late, so the shader module likely must be a sibling regular plugin) or the ShaderDirectoryMapper trick. (2) Many RDG/renderer types live in renderer-PRIVATE headers; a clean mod can do ENQUEUE_RENDER_COMMAND + FRDGBuilder + global compute/raster shaders, but injecting into the engine's own scene passes is not mod-clean. (3) The candidate already lists this as its top keyRisk and ships an FCanvas-per-tile fallback - correct. Do NOT take this path first; SceneCapture ortho-tiling + AbstractInstance reach the same TDR/VRAM goals with no shader infra. Reserve RDG for a later, profiled optimization.

techniques.name: UE::Tasks::Launch for off-game-thread gather / delta packing
techniques.whatItIs: Modern UE5 task API (UE::Tasks::Launch / FTask, pipes for ordering) preferred over FAsyncTask/TaskGraph for one-shot async work; first-class in 5.3.
techniques.appliesTo: asyncThreading (the candidate's worker-thread per-dirty-cell engine-transform gather and slim-record network-delta packing).
techniques.benefit: Clean primitive for the candidate's 'gather + pack on a worker, apply small mapped-buffer writes on the game thread' split. Lower overhead and simpler dependency expression than the legacy task graph; integrates with UE5Coro (already a dep) for the existing coroutine style.
techniques.caveats: Engine/UObject/scene-component touches (AddInstance, reading AFGBuildableSubsystem arrays, render-target ops) are NOT thread-safe and must stay on the game/render thread; only pure data transforms (packing FVector3f+yaw+classId into a byte blob) belong on the worker. Reading the engine's live buildable arrays off-thread races concurrent builds - snapshot per dirty cell on the game thread, hand the POD copy to the worker.

techniques.name: TSparseArray + TBitArray + FVector_NetQuantize / SerializeFixedVector (core engine primitives)
techniques.whatItIs: Stable-slot container with internal free list (TSparseArray), dirty-tile bitset (TBitArray), and built-in network quantizers: FVector_NetQuantize family (~20 bits/component) and SerializeFixedVector / FRotator::SerializeCompressed for fixed-bit position/yaw.
techniques.appliesTo: dataModel (TSparseArray slot = the candidate's stable handle; quantizers shrink the slim record on the wire); renderPipeline (TBitArray DirtyTiles); networkTransport (per-record wire size).
techniques.benefit: Every container the candidate names is core-engine and version-agnostic - no risk. The quantizers prove the ~28B slim record is real: classId (u16) + quantized FVector3f + compressed yaw fits well under 28B on the wire, and the existing NetSerialize already drops scale and quat, confirming the minimal record.
techniques.caveats: FVector_NetQuantize's ~+/-1,048,576 cm range covers the 750,000cm world with cm precision; pick the NetQuantize variant (or SerializeFixedVector bit count) to match the 1cm map resolution, not finer. TSparseArray slot reuse mandates the generation counter the candidate already specifies for ABA-safe network/UI handles.

techniques.name: Runtime Virtual Texture + Streaming Virtual Texture (for the zoom pyramid / overview mip)
techniques.whatItIs: RVT generates texel data on demand on the GPU; SVT streams baked low-res mips. Together they unify a high-res virtual surface with a streamed low-res overview, loading only visible pages.
techniques.appliesTo: renderPipeline (the candidate's 'fixed pyramid, residency cache, coarse overview mip, only on-screen tiles resident'); memoryModel (fixed VRAM ceiling independent of building count).
techniques.benefit: The candidate's bespoke 'tile atlas + residency cache + 1024^2 overview' is conceptually a virtual texture; RVT/SVT is the engine-native expression of exactly that 'load only visible pages, stream low mips' behavior and would give the fixed-VRAM-ceiling property without a hand-rolled residency manager.
techniques.caveats: RVT is designed around landscape/world-space material shading, not an arbitrary mod-drawn 2D atlas; bending it to a top-down map UI is non-idiomatic and RVT's own docs warn that rendering low mips over a large world is slow and forces actors resident. For a 4096^2 (64MB) or even 8192^2 fixed atlas the simple residency story is cheap enough that full RVT/SVT is likely over-engineering. Treat as 'available but probably not worth it' - a plain mip-chained render target + the SceneCapture overview is simpler and hits the same fixed-VRAM goal.

techniques.name: World Partition streaming sources for client area-of-interest alignment
techniques.whatItIs: UWorldPartitionStreamingSourceComponent: any actor can be a streaming source; sources compose (a cell in range of any source loads); per-source shapes and target_grid are configurable; streaming_source_enabled toggles at runtime. Satisfactory runs on World Partition (2D runtime hash grid).
techniques.appliesTo: networkTransport (the candidate's 'AoI driven by the client's map viewport + WP streaming source'); serverClientPartitioning (tiles map 1:1 to WP cells, chunk-load triggers a tile-version check).
techniques.benefit: Validates the candidate's AoI-streaming claim: the client's existing WP streaming sources already define which world region is resident, so the mod can align tile pulls to that region and get area-of-interest streaming 'for free' instead of pushing the whole dataset. Tile<->cell 1:1 mapping is realistic because both are fixed grids over the same fixed world bounds.
techniques.caveats: The map UI's view region and the player's WP streaming radius are NOT the same thing - opening the full map zoomed out makes AoI = whole world, so you still need the always-resident coarse overview mip for the zoomed-out case (the candidate already plans this). Reading/aligning to WP source state is read-only and safe; do not try to drive WP cell loading from the map - only consume the source positions to prioritize tile deltas.

modernizationRecommendations: Re-target the candidate's renderPipeline from a hand-rolled GPU-driven tiled compute rasterizer to a STOCK ENGINE PIPELINE that hits identical end-state guarantees with near-zero custom GPU code, then keep the data-model and network design almost verbatim. (1) RENDER: replace the 256x256 atlas + per-tile indirect/compute + custom RDG with one hidden marker actor holding per-CLASS AbstractInstance (ULightweightHISM) components + one USceneCaptureComponent2D (Orthographic, OrthoWidth=world width, CaptureSource=SceneColor, PrimitiveRenderMode=UseShowOnlyList, ShowOnlyActors=[marker actor], CaptureEveryFrame=false) into a 4096^2 RGBA8 target (64MB fixed); enable enable_orthographic_tiling with num_x_tiles/num_y_tiles so each debounced re-capture drains across frames as bounded submissions -> TDR structurally impossible, a built-in 5.3 feature. This one substitution dissolves the unbounded-GPU-pass root cause (#14), the 256MB target, the full-screen clear, the global FCanvas::GetBatchedElements hook, and the whole custom-shader keyRisk at once. (2) DATA MODEL: adopt AbstractInstance's FInstanceOwnerHandlePtr as the stable handle (it already gives slot+generation semantics, O(1) Add/RemoveInstance with internal swap-patch, and per-CLASS bucketing = ClassDrawTable); keep the slim SoA only on dedicated-server thin CLIENTS and engine-as-truth on the host; drop the separate Z-band index and instead ride worldZ+layerId in PerInstanceCustomData with a material clip() driven by MinZ/MaxZ+layer-mask scalars so the slider/layer toggles become O(1)+one re-capture. (3) SPATIAL INDEX: keep the candidate's uniform fixed-cell hash grid keyed by the stable handle for host dirty-cell gather and picking (AbstractInstance also offers ResolveHit/ResolveOverlap); kills the redirector/quadtree/reindex triad as intended. (4) NETWORK: keep the delta-by-tile-version design verbatim but implement it on the in-repo ReliableMessaging SendTaggedMessage(player, Cartograph.TileSync tag, payload); version = hash of authoritative tile content (not a session counter); use FVector_NetQuantize/SerializeFixedVector for the ~28B record; fixes #9 by construction. (5) ASYNC: keep monotonic dirty-set draining; move per-dirty-cell gather + delta packing to UE::Tasks::Launch workers (POD snapshots only), apply instance patches + trigger one debounced CaptureSceneDeferred on the game thread; no cancel/restart. (6) ENABLE DEPS: uncomment AbstractInstance and add ReliableMessaging in Cartograph.Build.cs; add the marker mesh/material content; no Niagara, no custom shader module, no PostConfigInit infra needed for this path. Net: the candidate's PHILOSOPHY (one source of truth, stable handles, cost bounded by viewport+frame) is correct and modern; the IMPLEMENTATION should lean on AbstractInstance + SceneCapture ortho-tiling + ReliableMessaging (all in-repo / in-engine on 5.3.2) instead of a from-scratch RDG rasterizer + custom transport. Hold the custom-RDG tiled compute path in reserve as a profiled, optional Phase-N optimization only if ortho-tiling capture proves too coarse for per-edit locality.
deprecatedApproaches: 1. CUSTOM GPU-DRIVEN TILED COMPUTE RASTERIZER VIA HAND-ROLLED RDG, as the FIRST/primary renderer: on a Default-LoadingPhase GameFeature mod with no Shaders dir, this needs net-new shader infrastructure (a PostConfigInit shader module or ShaderDirectoryMapper), wrestles renderer-private headers, and is the candidate's own #1 risk. SceneCapture2D's native enable_orthographic_tiling reaches the same 'bounded per-frame submission, TDR-impossible' guarantee on stock 5.3 with zero shaders. Not wrong, just premature - demote it to an optional, profiled optimization, not the foundation. 2. ANY FCanvas-based map renderer, including the candidate's own 'FCanvas-per-tile EndDraw fallback' as a long-term plan: the global SUBSCRIBE(FCanvas::GetBatchedElements) hook taxes every canvas in the game and downcasts arbitrary render batches (a cross-mod hazard the diagnosis flags). Moving to a SceneCapture + instanced-mesh marker layer deletes the FCanvas path and the global hook entirely. Keep FCanvas-per-tile only as a last-ditch no-shader fallback, not a target. 3. HAND-ROLLING the stable-handle instance store / GPU instance buffer / per-instance upload (the candidate's bespoke TSparseArray<record> + manual StructuredBuffer patching): AbstractInstance already provides stable handles, O(1) add/remove with swap-patch, per-class bucketed components, deferred dirty marking, and per-instance custom data - all tuned for this game at megabase scale. Reimplementing it is wasted effort and higher risk. 4. The hand-rolled RemoteCallObject transfer (the source of #9): superseded by the in-repo ReliableMessaging plugin. The int16 slice counter, the synchronous full Archive<<CurrentBuildingData, the unchecked TMap::Find(), and the FBufferWriter-in-a-TMap are all artifacts of rolling your own reliable bulk channel that the plugin already solves correctly. 5. A separate sorted Z-index structure (the candidate's coarse Z-band TArray<TArray<uint32>>): superseded by PerInstanceCustomData worldZ + material clip(); the Z value rides on the instance the engine already stores, so a parallel Z index is redundant memory and bookkeeping. 6. Bespoke virtual-texture-style residency/atlas manager: if a fixed 64MB (4096^2) atlas is acceptable, the elaborate per-tile residency cache + RVT/SVT machinery is over-engineering; a plain mip-chained render target + the always-resident coarse overview captured by SceneCapture hits the same fixed-VRAM ceiling far more simply.
netVerdict: Modern tooling makes this architecture STRONGER and, more importantly, exposes that most of it can be built from parts already in the repo and the 5.3 engine - turning a high-risk from-scratch GPU/transport project into a largely integration project. The candidate's diagnosis-aligned core is correct and should be kept almost verbatim: ONE source of truth (engine-as-truth on host), stable generational handles (no positional indices), O(1) mutation, cost bounded by viewport+frame. Every one of its root-cause fixes survives. The decisive modernization is that the renderPipeline's hardest, riskiest pieces are already solved on 5.3.2: (a) USceneCaptureComponent2D.enable_orthographic_tiling delivers the 'bounded per-frame GPU submission, TDR structurally impossible' killer-feature as a stock engine feature with ZERO custom shaders - confirmed present in the 5.3 API; (b) Satisfactory's own AbstractInstance plugin already provides the stable-handle, O(1), GPU-resident, per-class instanced store the candidate would otherwise hand-build; (c) PerInstanceCustomData + material clip() turns the O(N) Z/layer filter into O(1); and (d) the in-repo ReliableMessaging plugin's SendTaggedMessage fixes the #9 join crash by construction. Adopting these collapses the candidate's #1 keyRisk (custom RDG-from-a-mod) from a load-bearing dependency to an optional, profiled, later optimization - and the FCanvas-per-tile fallback can be dropped from the long-term plan entirely. There is NO fatal availability gap on the UE 5.3.2 CSS fork for the recommended path: every required primitive (SceneCapture ortho-tiling, ISM/HISM + GPU Scene auto-instancing under SM5/SM6, AbstractInstance, ReliableMessaging, TSparseArray/TBitArray, FVector_NetQuantize, UE::Tasks, WP streaming sources) is available without engine source changes. The only genuinely gated/frictional item is the custom global-shader/RDG path (partial: needs a PostConfigInit shader module or ShaderDirectoryMapper, and renderer-private headers limit how deep a mod can hook) - and the strong recommendation is precisely to NOT depend on it. Bottom line: keep the candidate's philosophy and data/network model; re-base its renderer on SceneCapture ortho-tiling + AbstractInstance instead of a bespoke RDG rasterizer, and the whole design becomes lower-risk, faster to ship, and fully buildable on 5.3.2 as a mod.

target: Atlas Tiled Streaming Map Pyramid (Cartograph, Satisfactory UE 5.3.2 CSS fork)

techniques.name: AbstractInstance LightweightHISM as stable-handle spatial/GPU store
techniques.whatItIs: In-repo Plugins/AbstractInstance: per-class LightweightHISM, AddInstance/RemoveInstance returning stable FInstanceOwnerHandlePtr, SetCustomPrimitiveDataOnHandle.
techniques.appliesTo: dataModel, renderPipeline, serverClientPartitioning
techniques.benefit: Stable O(1) handles (kills root cause 1), per-class bucketing (the per-class table), and HISM render-thread cluster culling for free. Per-instance custom data makes the Z-filter a material clip with zero per-event CPU.
techniques.caveats: Render representation, not a query DB; still need a hash grid keyed by handle for AOI. Add/remove are game-thread.

techniques.name: SceneCapture orthographic tiling, RVT/SVT pyramid, RetainerBox composite (renderer)
techniques.whatItIs: Ortho tiling (native UE 5.1, in 5.3) splits one ortho SceneCapture of the HISM into bounded sub-frames (SceneColor). RVT is the engine bounded page-pool mip pyramid with a per-frame upload cap; SVT is disk-backed. Composite via RetainerBox over a clear-disabled persistent pool; custom path uses RDG plus a scissored hardware clear per tile.
techniques.appliesTo: renderPipeline, asyncThreading (TDR), memoryModel, serverClientPartitioning (persistence)
techniques.benefit: Native no-single-unbounded-pass invariant (root cause 3 TDR): engine-bounded sub-frames make the 2-second TDR unreachable and delete the FCanvas hook. RVT is the Atlas bounded-page-pool pyramid (upload-cap CVAR equals tiles-per-frame); persistent pool fixes the 256MB clear; RetainerBox is about 10x faster than Canvas.
techniques.caveats: Ortho Beta 5.4, present 5.3; validate near/far on the CSS fork. RDG render-thread-only; version-gate RHI. RVT/SVT are material/cooker-driven, reference-only; realistic persistence is IFGSaveInterface content-hashed blobs with cold-bake fallback. Needs a GPU.

techniques.name: ReliableMessaging bulk channel (in-repo), verified against Atlas claims
techniques.whatItIs: In-repo: SendTaggedMessage and RegisterTaggedMessageHandler with a move-semantic rvalue byte-array delegate. Chunks at MaxPacketSize, int32 counts, ack-windowed reliable ordered delivery, late-handler queue. EOS/Steam/TCP.
techniques.appliesTo: networkTransport, serverClientPartitioning
techniques.benefit: Move-semantic payload, late-handler queue and int32 counters mean the whole issue-9 bug class (int16 slice overflow, move-unsafe buffer, stack-tail leak, per-join synchronous serialize) cannot exist by construction; the slice RCO is deleted. AOI pull is one send; steady state is coalesced per-tile version deltas.
techniques.caveats: Handle logout mid-transfer so a dropped client does not leak a pending stream. Confirm the bulk path on the live CSS network mode for multi-MB payloads. UE5Coro (vendored) gives off-thread tile encode/serialize, yielding per tile.

deprecatedApproaches: Delete slice RCO, FCanvas hook, 8192 monolith; reuse AbstractInstance.
netVerdict: Stronger except the headless dedicated-server gap: no GPU, so default to client-side baking from server slim lists (keyRisk 7).

target: Cartograph "Atlas" — Server-Authoritative Tiled Map Streaming. Re-architecture of the Satisfactory Cartograph mod (CSS UE 5.3.2 fork, SML, game 1.2). Evaluating how the latest engine/SDK tooling can make the candidate architecture cheaper/faster/leaner, flagging dated or unavailable techniques. Repo facts verified on disk: world bounds are constexpr (CartographGameInstanceModule.h:28-31); RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE=8192 (h:35); in-repo Plugins/ReliableMessaging is a real chunked/acked/windowed bulk transport over its own TCP/Steam/EOS transport layer (uint64 message ids, MTU chunking, per-chunk acks, FIFO priority queue, backpressure) but its public API is SendTaggedMessage(PC, FGameplayTag, TArray<uint8>) taking a whole in-RAM payload; in-repo Plugins/AbstractInstance exposes AAbstractInstanceManager with SetInstanceFromDataStatic/RemoveInstance (remove-swap O(1)), stable FInstanceOwnerHandlePtr handles, and SetCustomPrimitiveDataOnHandle for per-instance Z/layer data, but is COMMENTED OUT in Cartograph.Build.cs (line 49) and builds collision by default; UE5Coro is vendored into the mod, not the engine.

techniques.name: Scissored / sub-rect RHIClearRenderTargetView under RDG (kill the full-screen 67 M-texel opaque ClearItem)
techniques.whatItIs: Instead of the current full-size opaque FCanvasTileItem clear (256 MB write traffic on the 8192² target every redraw), bound the clear to the dirty tile/rect. The lowest-level form is RHICmdList.ClearRenderTargetView / RDG AddClearRenderTargetPass with a scissor (RHICmdList.SetScissorRect) sized to the dirty tile's page. Hardware fast-clear of a small sub-rect is effectively free vs rasterizing a screen-sized opaque quad through the batched-elements pixel pipeline.
techniques.appliesTo: renderPipeline (per-tile scissor-clear), asyncThreading (per-frame GPU bound)
techniques.benefit: A localized single-belt edit clears a few hundred pixels instead of 67 M texels; eliminates the per-pass 256 MB clear bandwidth that compounds the TDR. Per-tile 512² clear = 1 MB vs 256 MB (256x less clear traffic).
techniques.caveats: FCanvas does not expose a scissored hardware clear directly; the candidate's per-tile-page model already sidesteps this by clearing whole small pages. If staying on the global FCanvas hook, the clear must be issued as a scissor-clipped tile (correct but still goes through the batched pipeline). The clean form requires an RDG/RHI pass around the map's own EndDraw, which a mod CAN do via RenderCore (already a dependency) without engine changes.

techniques.name: Per-tile GPU command-buffer submission (Epic's official TDR-avoidance pattern) instead of one unbounded FCanvas flush
techniques.whatItIs: Epic's own UE 5.3 GPU-crash doc prescribes exactly the candidate's mechanism: split a large GPU job so 'each tile is submitted as a separate GPU command buffer ... This allows high quality rendering without triggering timeout detection' (their example is r.RayTracing.*.RenderTileSize). The Atlas per-tile dirty queue + EndDrawCanvasToRenderTarget/yield/re-Begin per MaxPrimitivesPerFrame is the same idea applied to the map raster: bounded RHI submissions spread over frames so no single submit approaches the ~2 s Windows TDR.
techniques.appliesTo: renderPipeline (hard GPU bound), asyncThreading (convergent dirty-tile queue)
techniques.benefit: Converts one ~0.5–1 M-primitive megabase submission (the verified #14 client-crash mechanism) into ceil(prims/budget) bounded submissions. Makes TDR structurally impossible by construction — this is the single highest-value correctness win and it is officially sanctioned.
techniques.caveats: The candidate's own keyRisk is real: a second BeginDrawCanvasToRenderTarget on the SAME persistent target must NOT implicitly re-clear (verify bClearRenderTarget=false path), or partial work is wiped each frame. EndDraw/Begin per K-prims has fixed per-flush overhead, so K should be tuned to amortize it (a few thousand+ prims/flush), not set to 1. Frame-relative budget (issue #10) must gate flush count too, else many tiny flushes still cost CPU.

techniques.name: Runtime Virtual Texture (RVT) in-game map pipeline
techniques.whatItIs: A modern alternative to the whole CPU-raster + monolithic-RT design: emit a stylized map color via RuntimeVirtualTextureOutput from the buildables' materials into an RVT volume covering the world, then sample it through an orthographic SceneCapture into the UI render target. RVT pages are GPU-generated on demand and streamed, giving page-level VRAM bounding and free LOD/mip — conceptually the candidate's tile pyramid but engine-native.
techniques.appliesTo: renderPipeline (tile pyramid / atlas / LOD), memoryModel (VRAM ceiling)
techniques.benefit: Page-streamed VRAM instead of a fixed 256 MB monolith; GPU generates only sampled pages; built-in mips for zoom. Eliminates the bespoke atlas/page-eviction machinery the candidate would otherwise hand-roll.
techniques.caveats: Designed for (mostly) STATIC geometry; the cited author warns moving/frequently-changing geometry makes 'the RVT struggle to keep up' — a factory under active build/dismantle is exactly the bad case, so RVT would need careful dirtying and is risky as the primary path. Requires the buildables to be drawn as real primitives with RVT output materials (i.e. an instanced marker layer), which only exists if the AbstractInstance path is adopted. RVT plumbing (volume, Draw-in-VT flags, material output) is available in 5.3 but the procedural-mesh ergonomics improved in 5.6+. Treat as an end-state option behind the instanced path, not a near-term primary.

techniques.name: AbstractInstance (in-repo) as the GPU-instanced marker layer with O(1) add/remove + per-instance custom data
techniques.whatItIs: Use the repo's AAbstractInstanceManager: one instanced component per buildable class on a hidden marker actor; SetInstanceFromDataStatic on build (returns a stable FInstanceOwnerHandlePtr), RemoveInstance on demolish (internal remove-swap → O(1), patches the moved handle), and SetCustomPrimitiveDataOnHandle to push worldZ/layerId for material-side Z-filter/layer clip(). This is the candidate's 'optional GPU-instanced end-state' — and it already exists, compiled, in the tree (just commented out in Build.cs).
techniques.appliesTo: renderPipeline (GPU-instanced path), dataModel (stable handles replace positional index), asyncThreading (no CPU redraw)
techniques.benefit: Add/remove become O(1) handle ops with NO redirector and NO O(N) reindex — dissolves the central root cause at the rendering layer. Z-filter/layer toggles become material-param/custom-data updates instead of O(N) array re-walks. Redraw cost moves to GPU instancing, independent of the CPU draw loop.
techniques.caveats: VERIFIED on disk but COMMENTED OUT in Cartograph.Build.cs:49 — must be re-enabled. AAbstractInstanceManager builds collision components by default (ULightweightCollisionComponent); a map-marker layer wants visual-only — set bUseBatchedCollision=false / a no-collision profile or you pay physics state for thousands of markers. It is FG's WORLD instancing system; isolating its render into a SceneCapture (not the real scene) needs ShowOnlyActors + GetViewOwner override (the Cartograph_2.0 branch's fragile mechanism). Handles are TSharedPtr (NotThreadSafe, game-thread only) — cannot mutate from the worker that builds snapshots. This is the candidate's own keyRisk #1; the canvas-tile path remains the safe primary.

techniques.name: Orthographic SceneCaptureComponent2D with UseShowOnlyList + enable_orthographic_tiling + lod_distance_factor
techniques.whatItIs: If rendering markers (AbstractInstance or RVT), capture them top-down with a single USceneCaptureComponent2D: PrimitiveRenderMode=UseShowOnlyList (ShowOnlyActors=marker actor) for isolation, bCaptureEveryFrame=false (capture only on a debounced dirty flag), enable_orthographic_tiling to split the ortho capture across frames (TDR-safe, pairs with SCS_SceneColor), and lod_distance_factor>1 to force cheaper LODs in the capture pass.
techniques.appliesTo: renderPipeline (capture = redraw), asyncThreading (debounced single capture vs cancel-restart)
techniques.benefit: One CaptureSceneDeferred() replaces the per-building FCanvas DrawItem loop and the per-primitive co_await; orthographic tiling gives a second engine-native TDR bound; LOD factor cuts zoomed-out cost. Debounced capture is the convergence model with zero hand-rolled coroutine cancellation.
techniques.caveats: enable_orthographic_tiling only applies when CaptureSource uses SceneColor (not FinalColor) per the API docs — constrains the post/material setup. SceneCapture takes a different (sometimes heavier) render route than the main view; a full ortho capture of a megabase each dirty-frame can itself hitch, so it MUST be debounced + dirty-gated, not per-event. GetViewOwner/show-only isolation under CSS's renderer fork is unverified (candidate keyRisk #1) — validate before committing.

techniques.name: ReliableMessaging bulk channel for AoI-scoped join streaming + per-tile version deltas
techniques.whatItIs: Replace the bespoke RCO slice protocol (verified #9: 3 unchecked TMap::Find null-derefs, int16 slice overflow at ~63 MB, full synchronous per-join serialize, reliable-multicast-per-event) with the in-repo ReliableMessaging: SendTaggedMessage(PC, Tag, blob) over its own chunked/acked transport (uint64 message ids, MTU-sized chunks, per-chunk acks, FIFO queue, backpressure via socket-full, keep-alives, per-player UReliableMessagingPlayerComponent keyed teardown).
techniques.appliesTo: networkTransport (join + deltas), serverClientPartitioning (AoI pull)
techniques.benefit: Kills #9 by construction: uint64 ids (no int16 overflow), windowed/acked transfer with backpressure (slow clients just receive slower), per-PlayerController component with disconnect teardown (no timeout-race null-deref, no per-join leak). Shared immutable ref-counted snapshot blobs make join O(joiners+AoI) instead of O(joiners·N).
techniques.caveats: VERIFIED in-repo source, but the candidate over-states it: (1) the public API SendTaggedMessage takes a whole TArray<uint8> by value — you must hold each tile blob fully in RAM to enqueue (fine for small per-tile blobs, NOT for one whole-dataset blob), which actually REINFORCES the per-tile design. (2) The send queue is strict FIFO, not priority-sorted — AoI-visible tiles can't preempt already-queued far tiles without app-level ordering. (3) It requires a transport layer (TCP/Steam/EOS) to be initialized and InitializeServer() called; adds a dependency and a handshake (Server_AdvertiseNewConnection round-trip) before first byte. (4) Tag registration costs a round-trip per new tag — use a small fixed tag set (manifest/tile/version), not a tag per tile.

techniques.name: UE::Tasks::Launch for off-game-thread snapshot serialization/compression and the initial bucketing pass
techniques.whatItIs: Run snapshot blob construction/compression and the one-time O(N) initial bucketing of engine buildables into grid cells on worker tasks via UE::Tasks::Launch (the modern 5.x task API, successor to raw FTaskGraphInterface), with only the final atomic snapshot-pointer + version swap on the game thread.
techniques.appliesTo: asyncThreading (off-game-thread work), serverClientPartitioning (load-time bucketing)
techniques.benefit: Removes the verified synchronous game-thread stalls (the O(N²) InitialBuildableGather, the by-value engine-map deep copy) from the critical path; snapshot build never blocks a frame. Replaces the bespoke vendored UE5Coro machinery for the pure-CPU, non-latent work where a task is simpler and cheaper than a coroutine frame.
techniques.caveats: Reading AFGBuildableSubsystem/AFGLightweightBuildableSubsystem live state from a worker is unsafe while the game thread mutates it — snapshot the inputs (slim records) on the game thread first, then process the immutable copy on the worker. UObject/handle (AbstractInstance) touches must stay on the game thread. Keep the existing UE5Coro/FTickTimeBudget for the latent, frame-budgeted draw drain; use UE::Tasks only for pure-data work.

techniques.name: TSparseArray stable-handle store + uniform hash grid + decoupled Z-index (kill the positional-index/redirector triad)
techniques.whatItIs: The data-model core the candidate already specifies and the diagnosis confirms as THE central fix: TSparseArray slot = stable BuildingId (O(1) add/remove, positions never shift), TMap<FIntPoint,TArray<BuildingId>> uniform grid over the constexpr bounds keyed by stable id (O(1) insert/erase, no redirector), and a separate sorted Z-index for the height slider. These are stock UE container facilities, fully available, no version gating.
techniques.appliesTo: dataModel (storage/spatial/Z split), memoryModel (leak elimination), asyncThreading (O(1) ingestion)
techniques.benefit: Dissolves all four CPU/memory root causes at once: O(N²) load → O(N); O(N)/event → O(1); the session-long never-compacting IndexRedirector leak → gone (live count, not lifetime); ~344–432 B/building second copy + ~152–192 B precomputed caches → ~24–28 B slim record (8–15×). Resident memory goes flat across a build/dismantle session (removes the #14 'worsens over ~1 h' signature).
techniques.caveats: Pure CONTAINER/algorithm work — no new tooling needed and nothing dated here; this is the load-bearing change and it is engine-version-agnostic. Risks are the candidate's own: dropping the global Z-sort needs per-tile Z-order at raster for overlap; single-precision FVector3f pos / float16 yaw forbid any exact-equality transform compares (the old value-quadtree identity); long belts/foundations must multi-insert into every overlapped grid cell consistently on move/remove.

techniques.name: IFGSaveInterface (ShouldSave) for persisting the tile-snapshot cache + grid + Z-index in the save
techniques.whatItIs: Persist the authoritative tile snapshots, per-tile versions, and grid via the engine's standard save path: implement IFGSaveInterface on the authoritative mod subsystem and return true from ShouldSave so the cache is serialized with the world and reloaded instead of re-bucketed from scratch.
techniques.appliesTo: serverClientPartitioning (compute-once-and-persist), memoryModel (disk trade)
techniques.benefit: Reload does not re-pay the O(N) bucketing; chunk-load is an O(1) cache lookup. Standard, supported mechanism — no custom save plumbing.
techniques.caveats: Embedding snapshot blobs bloats the save and risks format churn (candidate keyRisk): version-prefix every blob and keep a clean fallback to rebuild from engine arrays when the schema is stale. Persisting derived data that is cheaply recomputable is arguably premature — snapshots are a function of the (already-saved) factory, so persisting them trades save size for load time; make it optional/config and prefer persisting only the grid+slim records if save bloat is a concern.

techniques.name: World Partition cell-aligned tiling for O(1) chunk-load mapping
techniques.whatItIs: Size the 256 m map tiles to align with Satisfactory's World Partition cell granularity so 'client entered a new WP region' maps directly to 'pull these tile snapshots', making chunk-load an O(1) version lookup + optional blob fetch rather than any recompute.
techniques.appliesTo: serverClientPartitioning (AoI/chunk alignment), renderPipeline (tile grid sizing)
techniques.benefit: AoI streaming rides the engine's existing spatial streaming; far edits invalidate only their tile and never touch the client's current view. No bespoke region-tracking needed.
techniques.caveats: Satisfactory uses WP but the exact runtime cell size / streaming-source API surface usable from a mod on the CSS fork is unverified here — confirm the WP cell dimensions and whether a mod can observe cell load/unload events before hard-coupling tile size to WP cells. The map AoI is driven by the UI viewport (what the player is looking at on the map), which is NOT the same as the player's world streaming AoI — don't conflate them; the UI viewport rect should drive tile pulls.

techniques.name: FWidgetRenderer / Slate retained path instead of the global FCanvas::GetBatchedElements hook
techniques.whatItIs: The current design hooks FCanvas::GetBatchedElements GLOBALLY (taxes every canvas in the game, with an unchecked static_cast cross-mod hazard). Froyok's benchmark shows Canvas RT rendering is ~10× slower than a cached Slate FWidgetRenderer path (~12 ms vs ~1.3 ms for 50 RTs). For the map's own surface, a dedicated render pass (or the instanced SceneCapture) removes the process-wide hook entirely.
techniques.appliesTo: renderPipeline (draw mechanism), asyncThreading (per-frame cost)
techniques.benefit: Eliminates the system-wide per-batch trampoline + heap alloc + virtual dispatch + cross-mod downcast hazard on UI the mod never intended to touch; the map gets a cached, isolated draw path ~10× cheaper than the Canvas pipeline.
techniques.caveats: FWidgetRenderer can render a widget only once per frame (needs a pool for multiple updates) and is a UMG/Slate-shaped tool — it fits a widget-composited map, less so a per-building primitive raster. The cleaner end-state (instanced SceneCapture, or a dedicated RDG pass around the map RT) is the real fix for the global hook; FWidgetRenderer is one option, not mandatory. The key point is: STOP hooking GetBatchedElements globally regardless of which replacement is chosen.

modernizationRecommendations:
Adopt the Atlas data model wholesale — it is correct and almost all of it is plain stock-UE containers with no version risk — and layer the modern engine tooling onto it in this priority order:

1) DATA MODEL FIRST (available-ue532, no new tooling): TSparseArray stable-handle store + uniform hash grid keyed by stable id + decoupled Z-index + per-class ClassDrawTable + slim ~28 B record. This alone dissolves the four CPU/RAM root causes (O(N²) load, O(N)/event, redirector leak, second-copy). It is engine-version-agnostic and the highest-confidence, lowest-risk part of the whole plan. Do this before any rendering or network change; everything else builds on it.

2) GPU BOUND via the OFFICIAL pattern: implement the per-tile / per-K-primitive bounded-submission raster exactly as Epic's UE 5.3 GPU-crash doc prescribes ('each tile submitted as a separate GPU command buffer'). Pair the per-tile scissored hardware clear (RDG AddClearRenderTargetPass / RHI ClearRenderTargetView under SetScissorRect, via RenderCore which is already a Build.cs dep) to delete the 256 MB full-screen clear. This makes TDR structurally impossible and is the single biggest correctness win. Keep FTickTimeBudget for the CPU side; add MaxPrimitivesPerFrame for the GPU side — two independent ceilings.

3) NETWORK via in-repo ReliableMessaging, but design TO ITS REAL API: per-tile blobs (small enough to hold in RAM for SendTaggedMessage's by-value payload), a small FIXED gameplay-tag set (manifest/tile/version, not a tag-per-tile), app-level AoI ordering on top of its FIFO queue, and lean on its uint64 ids + per-PlayerController component teardown to kill #9 by construction. Initialize the transport layer + handshake at world load, not lazily at first join.

4) OFF-THREAD with UE::Tasks::Launch for snapshot serialization/compression and the one-time bucketing pass (snapshot immutable inputs on the game thread first, process on the worker, atomic pointer+version swap back). Keep the vendored UE5Coro only for the latent, frame-budgeted draw drain.

5) PERSISTENCE via IFGSaveInterface/ShouldSave, version-prefixed, with a rebuild-from-engine fallback; make snapshot persistence optional/config since snapshots are recomputable.

6) END-STATE rendering options, gated behind (1)-(2) landing and behind validation of CSS-fork SceneCapture isolation: re-enable the in-repo AbstractInstance (uncomment Build.cs:49, disable its collision) for O(1) AddInstance/RemoveInstance markers with per-instance custom-data Z/layer, captured by an orthographic SceneCaptureComponent2D (UseShowOnlyList + enable_orthographic_tiling + lod_distance_factor, bCaptureEveryFrame=false + debounced dirty capture). RVT-as-map is the most engine-native tiling but is static-geometry-oriented and risky for an actively-edited factory — treat it as a research spike, not the primary path. Either end-state lets you DELETE the global FCanvas::GetBatchedElements hook (a real cross-mod hazard and a ~10× Canvas tax).

Sequence: ship the data model + bounded-GPU + scissored-clear + ReliableMessaging join on the existing canvas-tile renderer (all available-ue532, all dissolve a verified root cause). Defer the AbstractInstance/SceneCapture and RVT paths to a gated end-state once CSS-fork capture isolation is proven.
deprecatedApproaches:
- GLOBAL FCanvas::GetBatchedElements hook: process-wide tax on every canvas, heap alloc + virtual dispatch per batch, and an unchecked static_cast of an arbitrary render batch (cross-mod crash hazard). Dated mechanism to apply a scissor that is only needed for ONE surface; modern path is a dedicated RDG/RHI pass around the map RT, or rendering markers via instancing+SceneCapture so there is no FCanvas path at all (Froyok: Canvas ~10× slower than cached Slate).
- The 8192² RGBA8 monolith with bAutoGenerateMips: a fixed 256 MB VRAM floor independent of factory size, plus a whole-texture auto-mip pass every redraw that silently defeats the scissor. Superseded by a fixed-budget tile atlas (or RVT page streaming) with lazy per-page mips only while the map is open.
- One unbounded FCanvas open across the whole redraw, flushed once: the verified TDR/client-crash mechanism (#14). Directly contradicts Epic's own 5.3 guidance to split GPU work into per-tile command buffers. Deprecated by construction.
- Positional indices into a Z-sorted array + the never-compacting BuildingDataIndexRedirector + TQuadTree<int32>: the central O(N²)/O(N)/leak triad. The redirector exists ONLY because TQuadTree<int32> can't update payloads and the array renumbers on insert; both disappear with TSparseArray stable handles + a uniform grid keyed by handle. There is no modern reason to keep a positional-index quadtree for this workload.
- Storing a full second FBuildingData copy with ~152–192 B of PRECOMPUTED draw caches (ScreenPosition/Corners/Rotation/VisualBoxCache): all recomputable in tens of FLOPs from Transform + a per-class lookup; the corner math is even computed twice today. Caching derived data per-building, 1 M times, is the dated choice; recompute-on-raster against a per-class table is correct.
- The bespoke RCO slice protocol (int16 slice count overflow at ~63 MB, 3 unchecked TMap::Find null-derefs, full synchronous per-join whole-dataset serialize, NetMulticast-Reliable-per-build-event, move-unsafe FBufferWriter-in-a-TMap): every one of these is obviated by the in-repo ReliableMessaging (uint64 ids, chunked/acked/backpressured, per-PlayerController teardown). Hand-rolling a reliable large-payload transport when a purpose-built one ships in the same repo is the dated decision.
- co_await Budget per individual primitive (every spline segment, every rectangle edge): millions of awaiter evaluations + a Cycles() read per primitive. The FTickTimeBudget MODEL is correct (frame-relative, the right answer to issue #10) but the GRANULARITY is dated — await per tile / per K buildings, and add a separate GPU primitive cap.
netVerdict:
Modern tooling makes this architecture STRONGER and exposes NO fatal availability gap — every load-bearing technique is available on the CSS UE 5.3.2 fork, and several are not just available but engine-native and officially sanctioned. The two highest-value claims are independently confirmed by primary sources: (1) Epic's own UE 5.3 GPU-crash documentation prescribes exactly the candidate's TDR fix — split GPU work so each tile is a separate command buffer — so the per-tile bounded-submission raster is the officially-correct pattern, not a gamble; and (2) the in-repo ReliableMessaging is, on inspection of its source, a genuine chunked/acked/windowed/backpressured bulk transport with uint64 message ids and per-PlayerController teardown, which dissolves the verified #9 join-crash mechanisms by construction. The data-model core (TSparseArray stable handles + uniform grid + decoupled Z-index + slim record) is plain stock-UE containers with zero version risk and is the single highest-confidence change.

The architecture's own self-identified primary/fallback split is exactly right and the research reinforces it: keep the bounded canvas-tile raster as the PRIMARY (all available-ue532), and gate the GPU-instanced end-state. Three concrete adjustments fall out of the verification, none fatal: (a) ReliableMessaging's public API takes a whole in-RAM payload and is strict-FIFO — which actually REINFORCES the per-tile blob design but requires a small fixed tag set, app-level AoI ordering, and early transport-layer init; the candidate slightly over-states it as turnkey 'BulkDataReplication'. (b) The AbstractInstance end-state is real and in-tree but is COMMENTED OUT in Build.cs, builds collision by default, uses game-thread-only TSharedPtr handles, and depends on UNVERIFIED SceneCapture render-isolation on CSS's renderer fork — correctly the candidate's #1 keyRisk, correctly gated. (c) RVT-as-map is the most engine-native tiling primitive but is static-geometry-oriented and the cited practitioner explicitly warns it 'struggles to keep up' with changing geometry, so it is a research spike, not the primary path for an actively-edited factory. Net: adopt as designed, build the network layer to ReliableMessaging's real (per-tile) API rather than an idealized bulk API, and defer the instanced/SceneCapture/RVT rendering to a validated end-state. The plan is sound and the tooling is there.

target: Tessera — Stable-Handle Incremental Tile Compositor (candidate re-architecture of the Cartograph mod for Satisfactory on Coffee Stain's UE 5.3.2 fork)

techniques.name: FSlateDrawElement::MakeCustomVerts with hardware-instanced buffer (custom SLeafWidget map renderer)
techniques.whatItIs: Instead of FCanvas→UCanvasRenderTarget2D raster, draw the map in a custom Slate leaf widget's OnPaint by building one (or a few) FSlateVertex/index batch(es) and submitting them via FSlateDrawElement::MakeCustomVerts(OutDrawElements, Layer, ResourceHandle, Verts, Indices, InstanceData, InstanceOffset, InstanceCount). The overload takes an instance buffer + instance count, i.e. true per-instance hardware instancing of a unit quad/line for every building, batched into ONE Slate draw element and one RHI draw. The widget paints directly to the on-screen map panel; no intermediate 256 MB render target, no full-screen clear, no FCanvas re-creation per frame.
techniques.appliesTo: renderPipeline, asyncThreading, memoryModel (VRAM), the whole 'persistent tile pyramid' subsystem
techniques.benefit: Froyok's measured Canvas-vs-Slate benchmark: ~12 ms (Canvas/RT) vs ~1.3 ms (Slate) for the same work — roughly 10x render-thread cost, because FCanvas is rebuilt and not cached every draw. MakeCustomVerts collapses N buildings into 1 draw call via the instance buffer, and eliminates the entire VRAM render target (Tessera's 64 MB tile pyramid → 0 MB persistent target; the on-screen panel is composited by Slate's own swap-chain pass). Also removes the global FCanvas::GetBatchedElements hook entirely — the widget is the mod's own, so no process-wide canvas tax.
techniques.caveats: MakeCustomVerts geometry is NOT depth-sorted across instances within a batch, so the Z-band draw order Tessera relies on must be baked into the vertex/instance ordering (paint back-to-front) — exactly the ordering the new Z-band index already produces, so this is a natural fit, not a regression. Slate culls by the widget clip rect, not a tile grid, so the 'tile pyramid + dirty-tile bitset' machinery becomes partly redundant: instead of compositing tiles into a texture, you'd cull instances to the visible viewport and let Slate's invalidation/retainer cache the result. A custom SLeafWidget + MakeCustomVerts is more engine-surface than 'pure UCanvasRenderTarget2D', contradicting Tessera's stated minimalism — but it is still 100% public Slate API, no engine source changes. Zoom LOD (Tessera's mip pyramid) must be re-expressed as instance-count culling per zoom rather than texture mips. This is the single highest-value modernization but it partially rewrites renderPipeline rather than tuning it.

techniques.name: Persistent render target via UpdateResourceImmediate(bShouldClearRenderTargetOnReceiveUpdate=false) + scissored RHIClearRenderTargetView
techniques.whatItIs: If the canvas-to-RT pipeline is kept (Tessera's stated design), the persistent-target requirement is satisfied by UCanvasRenderTarget2D::RepaintCanvas → UpdateResourceImmediate(false), which skips the per-update clear and preserves prior contents across draws. Per-tile incremental clears are done with RHICmdList.SetScissorRect(...) + RHICmdList.ClearRenderTargetView(...) inside an ENQUEUE_RENDER_COMMAND, a free hardware clear bounded to the tile rect, replacing the full-screen opaque FCanvasTileItem.
techniques.appliesTo: renderPipeline (persistent tile pyramid, scissored clear), memoryModel (clear bandwidth)
techniques.benefit: Confirms Tessera's two load-bearing render claims are reachable from a mod with zero engine changes: (1) the 2nd BeginDraw will NOT implicitly clear when the preserve flag is false, so the persistent pyramid is real; (2) a scissored hardware clear touches ≤256 KB per tile instead of the 67 M-texel / ~256 MB full-screen opaque clear per redraw. The mod already calls RHICmdList.SetScissorRect in CartographCanvasRenderItem.cpp, so the RHI surface is proven-reachable in this exact codebase.
techniques.caveats: bShouldClearRenderTargetOnReceiveUpdate lives on the UCanvasRenderTarget2D path; verify the exact UE 5.3.2 CSS-fork signature of UpdateResourceImmediate before relying on it (the flag exists in stock UE but CSS forks occasionally diverge in Engine/Source). bAutoGenerateMips MUST be disabled on the asset or EndDraw kicks a full-texture mip pass every redraw that silently defeats the scissor (a separately-verified render finding). This technique only matters if you keep the RT pipeline; if you adopt MakeCustomVerts (technique 1) the persistent RT and its clear disappear entirely, making this moot. Scissored ClearRenderTargetView is a render-thread op — it must be enqueued, adding a GT→RT hop the immediate-mode canvas path did not have.

techniques.name: TSparseArray stable-slot store + generational handle (identity decoupled from array position)
techniques.whatItIs: Tessera's core: replace the Z-sorted TArray + TQuadTree<int32> + BuildingDataIndexRedirector with TSparseArray<FSlimRecord> where the slot index is the stable identity, paired with a uint16 generation for ABA safety. TSparseArray gives O(1) Add at the lowest free index (EmplaceAtLowestFreeIndex), O(1) RemoveAt with free-list reuse, and indices that never shift.
techniques.appliesTo: dataModel (single source of identity), complexityTable (per-event O(N)→O(1), load O(N^2)→O(N))
techniques.benefit: Directly deletes the verified central root cause: the O(N) redirector reindex per add/remove, the O(N^2) initial load, and the never-compacting tombstone leak all collapse because positions never move and removal frees the slot in O(1). This is the highest-ROI change and it is a stock UE container — no exotic tooling, no version risk. Confirmed semantics: TSparseArray is 'O(1) element removal' with a managed free list.
techniques.caveats: TSparseArray slot reuse is exactly why Tessera's generation tag is mandatory — any net/UI path that holds a BuildingId across remove+add will read a recycled slot without it (already in Tessera's keyRisks, correctly). TSparseArray's allocation block is not contiguous-iterable as cheaply as TArray for the draw loop; the draw path should iterate via the spatial-grid/Z-band query results (which is what Tessera does), not by walking the sparse array, or cache locality suffers. No availability risk — this is the safest part of the whole design.

techniques.name: ReliableMessaging (CSS 'BulkDataReplication') tagged large-payload transport — in-repo plugin
techniques.whatItIs: Replace the hand-rolled RCO slice protocol with the repo's ReliableMessaging plugin: UReliableMessagingSubsystem::SendTaggedMessage(PC, FGameplayTag, TArray<uint8>) on the server, UReliableMessagingPlayerComponent::RegisterTaggedMessageHandler(Tag, FOnBulkDataReplicationPayloadReceived) on the client. It runs over a dedicated side-channel net connection (TCP, EOS-P2P, or Steam-P2P) and internally chunks/acks/reassembles (RDTProtocol with CurrentChunkSize/ChunkHeader.Length), off the gameplay reliable channel.
techniques.appliesTo: networkTransport, serverClientPartitioning, complexityTable (join row)
techniques.benefit: Confirmed by reading the plugin source: the int16 slice-overflow class vanishes by construction because RDTProtocol::SizeType = TArray<uint8>::SizeType (int32 on 64-bit), so message/chunk lengths are 32-bit, not int16. Chunking+ack+backpressure are built in, removing the per-join full synchronous serialize, the reliable-multicast-per-event flood, and the channel-saturation class. The TCP transport module (ReliableMessagingTCP) depends only on Sockets+OnlineSubsystemUtils and is NOT in the Server TargetDenyList, so it links on the dedicated-server target where the EOS/Steam P2P modules are denied — the dedicated-server join path (#9) is covered.
techniques.caveats: VERIFIED IN-REPO, not from public web (this is a CSS-internal plugin, no external docs exist — sources field points only to general UE context). Real caveats from the source: (1) SendTaggedMessage takes the payload BY VALUE (TArray<uint8> InPayload) — Tessera's shared-ref FTileSnapshot must be copied into the payload at send time, so the 'O(N) total server memory, shared-ref pinned by all joiners' claim holds for the cache but each in-flight send still materializes a per-recipient byte copy; size the in-flight window accordingly. (2) The connection handshake (Connecting→Connected, EReliableMessagingConnectionState) must complete before the first tile send — Tessera's keyRisk about this is real; queue tiles until the player component reports Connected. (3) ConnectionTimeoutSeconds defaults to 20s; AoI streaming must keep sends flowing or idle connections can drop. Keep the hardened-RCO fallback behind a flag as Tessera proposes.

techniques.name: Uniform spatial hash grid over compile-time world bounds (replacing TQuadTree<int32>)
techniques.whatItIs: Tessera's flat TArray<TArray<uint32>> of fixed cells keyed by stable handle, replacing the quadtree. O(cells-covered) insert/erase, O(result) region query, no node splitting, no 40 B FBox2D/element, no redirector.
techniques.appliesTo: dataModel (spatial index), complexityTable (region redraw, mass-dismantle)
techniques.benefit: Removes the quadtree's 40 B/element FBox2D and the redirector's reason-to-exist. For a fixed-bounds, write-heavy, query-by-radius workload (verified as the actual access pattern) a uniform grid is strictly better than a persistent quadtree keyed by unstable ids — the arch audit independently reached this same conclusion (hashgrid-vs-quadtree finding). Pure CPU data structure, zero engine/tooling dependency, zero version risk.
techniques.caveats: Plain-STL/UE-container technique, not an engine feature — 'available' is trivially true. The verified risks are tuning, not availability: long belts / huge foundations span many cells (Tessera's ~64 m default + oversized-overflow-list mitigation is correct). The grid assumes fixed WEST/EAST/NORTH/SOUTH bounds; modded/expanded worlds need the overflow cell Tessera already lists. Satisfactory uses World Partition, so aligning grid cells to WP cells (Tessera's serverClientPartitioning) is sound and lets AoI eviction reuse engine streaming boundaries.

techniques.name: RDG (FRDGBuilder) custom pass via ENQUEUE_RENDER_COMMAND — for an optional GPU compositor
techniques.whatItIs: If a GPU-side tile compositor or a compute-driven clear/blit is ever wanted, RDG is reachable from the mod: allocate an FRDGBuilder inside ENQUEUE_RENDER_COMMAND on the render thread and add raster/compute passes that write sub-regions of a pooled render target. Lets you express Tessera's 'budgeted dirty-tile drain' as RDG passes with automatic resource lifetime/barriers.
techniques.appliesTo: renderPipeline (GPU-bounded compositing), asyncThreading (off-GT work)
techniques.benefit: Modern, barrier-correct alternative to hand-managed RHI clears if the compositor grows beyond simple scissored clears; RDG pools transient allocations and prunes unused passes. Available in 5.3 — FRDGBuilder is constructed from an immediate command list inside a render command.
techniques.caveats: Marked partial because FRDGBuilder is render-thread-ONLY — it cannot be driven from the game thread directly; you must bridge via ENQUEUE_RENDER_COMMAND, and FRDGBuilderRecorder (the GT-side queuing helper) is a LATER-UE addition not guaranteed on 5.3.2. For Tessera's stated 'pure-canvas, minimal engine surface' philosophy this is OVERKILL: scissored ClearRenderTargetView (technique 2) or MakeCustomVerts (technique 1) cover the need without RDG. Recommend RDG only as a contingency if the budgeted compositor must do GPU work the canvas/Slate paths can't express. Adds meaningful engine-surface and shader-management burden to a mod.

techniques.name: ISM/HISM + USceneCaptureComponent2D marker renderer (the Cartograph_2.0 direction) — REJECTED, dated
techniques.whatItIs: The previously-explored alternative: place each building as an instance in per-class HISM on a hidden marker actor and capture it top-down with an orthographic SceneCapture2D; add/remove = AddInstance/RemoveInstance, redraw = one CaptureSceneDeferred.
techniques.appliesTo: renderPipeline, dataModel (would replace the slim store with engine instance arrays)
techniques.benefit: Would, in theory, move rasterization to the GPU and make redraw fixed-cost. Listed here because Stage-1 flagged it as a 'validated direction (Phase 5)' — the modern evidence REVERSES that for the megabase target.
techniques.caveats: DEPRECATED for this workload. UE5's ISM/HISM AddInstance/RemoveInstance regressed hard vs UE4: community-reported 'basically unusable after 10,000 instances' incrementally, and 250k instances taking 5 min in 5.7 vs 10 s in 4.27 — root cause is Chaos collision rebuild on every instance mutation (mitigable by disabling collision + batch AddInstances, but the render-state-dirty cost remains). For Cartograph's 200k–1M buildings with hot per-event add/remove (issue #14's exact trigger) this path would re-introduce the very hitches it's meant to cure. SceneCapture2D also needs a 2nd scene-color/HDR target (can WORSEN the VRAM story). 'needs-newer-ue' tag reflects that ISM mutation cost is only acceptable on UE versions with the post-5.4 GPUScene/instance-update improvements — and even there, not at 1M with per-frame churn. Tessera is correct to NOT adopt this; downgrade Stage-1's 'Phase 5 end-state' framing.

techniques.name: UE 5.5 async Slate RDG execution + parallel RHI translation (up to 2x) — NOT on the fork
techniques.whatItIs: UE 5.5 added asynchronous RDG execute tasks that run ~half of Slate rendering async, plus parallel translation issuing RHI tasks for up to 2x throughput and fewer stalls.
techniques.appliesTo: renderPipeline, asyncThreading (the frame-relative budget would benefit)
techniques.benefit: Would roughly halve the cost of the Slate-based map render (technique 1) and reduce render-thread stalls — directly amplifying the MakeCustomVerts win and the frame-budget convergence.
techniques.caveats: 5.5 ONLY — the CSS fork is 5.3.2, so this is unavailable and must be explicitly version-gated. Listed so the design does NOT assume it. The Tessera frame-relative budget must therefore pace against 5.3's synchronous Slate/RHI cost model, not 5.5's async one. If CSS ever rebases the fork, technique 1's headroom roughly doubles for free; until then, budget conservatively.

techniques.name: FVector3f single-precision slim record + side-table SoA for extras
techniques.whatItIs: Tessera's 24 B FSlimRecord (uint32 ClassHash + FVector3f pos + float16 yaw + uint8 type + uint16 extraIndex) with spline/wire/beam polylines in side tables, recomputing all screen geometry at draw from a per-class FClassDrawInfo table.
techniques.appliesTo: dataModel, memoryModel (per-record 344-432 B → 24 B), complexityTable
techniques.benefit: 14–18x per-record shrink; eliminates the ~152–192 B derived cache and the duplicated corner math (the verified second-copy + precomputed-cache root causes). The wire format (NetSerialize already drops scale+quat, sends hash+pos+yaw) independently proves 24 B is sufficient. FVector3f is a stock 5.3 type; no tooling risk.
techniques.caveats: Single-precision FVector3f gives ~0.05 cm worst-case error at the 7.5 km map edge — visually irrelevant at 1 cm/px, BUT it forbids any exact-equality position compare (Tessera's keyRisk is correct; identity is the handle now, so this is fine). ComputeDrawGeometry must reproduce the old FillInCache math pixel-identically or icons shift — extract one shared pure helper, diff-render a large save, then delete stored fields (Tessera's mitigation is the right process). float16 yaw is adequate for a top-down map but confirm the half<->float path matches the existing compressed-yaw NetSerialize quantization so host and client agree.

modernizationRecommendations:
Concrete upgrades to THIS architecture, ordered by leverage:

1. KEEP the entire data-model half of Tessera as-is — it is the correct end-state and every primitive is stock-5.3, zero-risk: TSparseArray + generation (deletes the redirector/O(N^2)/leak — the verified central flaw), uniform hash grid (the arch audit reached the same conclusion independently), decoupled Z-band index, per-class FClassDrawInfo + draw-time ComputeDrawGeometry (deletes the second copy + precomputed caches), 24 B FVector3f slim record, convergent never-cancel-restarted debounced compositor with a frame-relative budget that awaits once-per-tile/per-K-buildings (not per-primitive). No modernization needed here; ship it.

2. REPLACE the render half. Tessera's stated 'pure UCanvasRenderTarget2D' is the one place where the latest tooling is materially better than the chosen design. Froyok's benchmark shows FCanvas→RT is ~10x the render-thread cost of Slate because FCanvas is rebuilt per draw and never cached. The modern primitive is a custom SLeafWidget whose OnPaint emits FSlateDrawElement::MakeCustomVerts with an instance buffer: every building becomes one instance of a unit quad/line, batched into ONE Slate draw element and ONE instanced RHI draw, painted straight to the on-screen map panel. This deletes, by construction: the 64 MB (or 256 MB) persistent render target and ALL its VRAM, the full-screen clear, the global FCanvas::GetBatchedElements process-wide hook (the widget is the mod's own), and the GT→RT canvas plumbing. The frame-relative budget then paces instance-buffer construction (cheap CPU) and Slate invalidation rather than canvas DrawItem emission. Net: VRAM 64 MB → ~0 persistent, render-thread cost ~10x lower, fewer engine hooks — strictly leaner than the tile pyramid on every axis.

3. If, and only if, you keep the RT pipeline (e.g. you need a persistent zoomable mip texture for the open-map UI, or MakeCustomVerts ordering/text proves awkward), then Tessera's persistent pyramid is fully reachable on 5.3.2 via UpdateResourceImmediate(bShouldClearRenderTargetOnReceiveUpdate=false) for content preservation + scissored RHIClearRenderTargetView for per-tile clears (the mod already calls SetScissorRect, so it's proven-reachable). Disable bAutoGenerateMips on the asset or it defeats the scissor.

4. ADOPT ReliableMessaging exactly as Tessera proposes — verified in-repo: SizeType is int32 so the int16 overflow is gone by construction, chunk/ack/backpressure are built in, and the TCP transport links on the dedicated-server target (EOS/Steam P2P are denied there). Two source-verified adjustments: SendTaggedMessage copies the payload by value (size the in-flight tile window with that copy cost in mind), and gate the first send on the connection reaching Connected state. Keep the hardened-RCO fallback behind a feature flag.

5. DO NOT use RDG unless a future GPU compositor outgrows scissored clears / MakeCustomVerts — it is render-thread-only, adds shader-management burden, and contradicts the minimal-engine-surface goal. Hold it as a documented contingency.
deprecatedApproaches:
1. The FCanvas → UCanvasRenderTarget2D immediate-mode raster pipeline itself is the dated core that Tessera unfortunately preserves and doubles down on ('evolve the canvas correctly instead of replacing it'). The modern primitive — FSlateDrawElement::MakeCustomVerts with an instance buffer in a custom Slate widget — is ~10x cheaper on the render thread (Froyok) and eliminates the persistent VRAM target entirely. Tessera's tile-pyramid + dirty-tile-bitset + scissored-clear machinery is a sophisticated workaround for a problem (the full-screen clear and unbounded single submission) that a Slate-instanced renderer does not have in the first place. Keep the tile/dirty-region CONCEPT for CPU-side culling and budgeted convergence, but the IMAGE should be Slate-instanced geometry, not a composited render target.

2. The global SUBSCRIBE(FCanvas::GetBatchedElements) hook (process-wide canvas tax + cross-mod static_cast hazard) — Tessera already deletes this, correctly; it is fully obviated by a mod-owned Slate widget.

3. The ISM/HISM + SceneCapture2D marker approach (Cartograph_2.0, which Stage-1 framed as the 'true end-state / Phase 5'). Modern UE5 evidence reverses this: ISM/HISM AddInstance/RemoveInstance regressed badly post-UE4 (community: 'unusable after 10k instances' incrementally; 250k = 5 min on 5.7 vs 10 s on 4.27) due to Chaos collision rebuilds and render-state-dirty cost. For 200k–1M buildings with hot per-event churn this is strictly worse than immediate-mode. Tessera correctly avoids it; the Stage-1 'Phase 5 end-state' recommendation should be downgraded to 'rejected for this workload'.

4. The hand-rolled RCO slice protocol (int16 slice count, null-deref Find, fixed-2047 NetSerialize, reliable-multicast-per-event, per-join full synchronous serialize) — Tessera correctly replaces it wholesale with ReliableMessaging; this is verified dead.

5. The Z-sorted master array + positional-index quadtree + IndexRedirector triad — the verified central flaw; Tessera deletes it via TSparseArray + hash grid + separate Z-band. No modern tooling needed, just correct data structures.
netVerdict: Modern tooling makes this architecture STRONGER, and exposes NO new fatal availability gap — every load-bearing primitive Tessera depends on is confirmed reachable on the UE 5.3.2 CSS fork without engine source changes (TSparseArray, FVector3f, uniform-grid containers, persistent-RT preserve flag, scissored RHIClearRenderTargetView, and the in-repo ReliableMessaging whose int32 SizeType kills the int16 overflow by construction and whose TCP transport links on the dedicated-server target). The data-model half of Tessera is the correct, ship-it end-state and needs no modernization. The single substantive finding is on the render half: Tessera's deliberate choice to PRESERVE the FCanvas→render-target pipeline is the one place the latest tooling beats the chosen design — a custom Slate widget emitting FSlateDrawElement::MakeCustomVerts with a per-instance buffer is ~10x cheaper on the render thread (Froyok), batches all buildings into one instanced draw, and deletes the persistent VRAM target, the full-screen clear, and the global canvas hook outright, making the elaborate tile-pyramid/dirty-bitset compositor largely unnecessary as an IMAGE store (though its CPU-side dirty-region culling and frame-relative budget remain valuable). Tessera also correctly REJECTS the two dated paths (ISM/SceneCapture, hand-rolled RCO) that modern evidence confirms are wrong for a 1M-building, high-churn workload — so the Stage-1 'Phase 5 ISM end-state' framing should be downgraded. Recommendation: adopt Tessera's data model verbatim; swap its render pipeline from canvas-tile-compositing to Slate-instanced MakeCustomVerts (falling back to the persistent-RT-preserve + scissored-clear design only if a persistent zoomable texture is genuinely required); adopt ReliableMessaging with the by-value-payload and connection-handshake caveats; hold RDG as a contingency only. Net at 1M buildings the design's targets (heap ~360–430 MB → ~26–38 MB, per-event O(N)→O(1), load O(N^2)→O(N), crash-free backpressured join) all stand, and the VRAM target improves further from 64 MB to ~0 persistent if the Slate-instanced renderer is adopted. One version gate to record: UE 5.5's async-Slate/parallel-RHI ~2x speedup is NOT on the 5.3.2 fork, so the frame budget must be tuned against 5.3's synchronous cost model.

target: Cartograph (Satisfactory factory-map mod) on Coffee Stain UE 5.3.2 fork via SML. SOTA UE5 rendering and data-structure tooling for a dynamic, mutation-heavy top-down 2D factory map (CPU/GPU/RAM/VRAM/network), with mod-from-plugin availability tags for 5.3.2.
modernizationRecommendations:
Stage the redesign so each layer is independently shippable and the data model is fixed before any renderer change.

CORE (must, no engine dependency, highest ROI): Replace the Z-sorted TArray FBuildingData plus TQuadTree int32 plus BuildingDataIndexRedirector triad with (1) a TSparseArray slim-record stable-handle store, (2) a uniform spatial hash grid over the fixed world bounds keyed by that handle, and (3) a separate Z-index (sorted pairs or 1m Z-bands). Shrink the resident record from ~344-432B to ~24-40B (classHash, FVector3f pos, yaw, type, extraIndex; spline/wire/beam payloads in side-tables) and DELETE all precomputed draw caches (FNormalDataCache/FRectangleDataCache/VisualBoxCache); recompute geometry at draw time from a per-CLASS table built once. On a host, the engine already holds every transform (AFGBuildableSubsystem, AFGLightweightBuildableSubsystem), so the host can drop the store entirely and iterate engine arrays per dirty cell; only dedicated-server clients keep the slim store. This alone makes per-event O(1), kills the redirector leak and the O(N^2) load, and is the prerequisite for everything else.

RENDERER END-STATE (recommended): per-class HISM marker layer plus orthographic USceneCaptureComponent2D with NATIVE bEnableOrthographicTiling (5.3 built-in) plus CaptureSceneDeferred on a debounced dirty flag. Biggest structural win, working WITH the engine grain (this is CSS AbstractInstance); add/remove become O(1) AddInstance/RemoveInstance, rasterization moves to the GPU, and orthographic tiling structurally eliminates the 2s TDR with zero engine-source changes. Encode worldZ/layerId in per-instance custom data and do Z/layer filtering as material clip() plus scalar params (filter change becomes 2 param writes plus one capture, not an O(N) full redraw). Delete the global FCanvas::GetBatchedElements hook and the scissor render item.

BRIDGE (ship first if the SceneCapture rewrite needs art review): keep the FCanvas path but (a) chunk the flush, Begin/End every ~20k primitives on a persistent never-fully-cleared target across NextTick, and (b) scissor the clear to the dirty bounds. Bounds the GPU submission (kills the TDR) and slashes clear bandwidth surgically. Froyok shows FCanvas is ~10x heavier than cached/instanced paths, so this is a bridge, not the destination.

UI: wrap the map widget in an SRetainerWidget with Phase throttling so presentation cost is decoupled from game framerate; Invalidation panels for static chrome.

NETWORK: reuse the repo ReliableMessaging plugin for a single shared, dirty-invalidated snapshot streamed with a multi-MTU pull window and int32 slice counts; the slim record makes the payload 8-15x smaller. Null-guard the RCO TMap::Find derefs and key cleanup on PlayerController logout to close #9 immediately.

ADVANCED (only if megabase frame time still does not hold): a bespoke compute/raster RDG rasterizer registered from the plugin (AddShaderSourceDirectoryMapping plus FSceneViewExtensionBase, confirmed no-engine-source), optionally on the async compute queue. VRAM: drop the target to 4096^2 (256MB to 64MB) regardless of renderer; RVT is a possible far-zoom static-pyramid layer ONLY (it struggles with the mutation-heavy live layer).
deprecatedApproaches:
