1. Positional-index quadtree plus IndexRedirector (the central flaw): storing array positions as spatial-index payload, kept valid by an O(N) never-compacting redirector. Modern primitive is stable handles (TSparseArray slot / generational handle) plus a spatial index keyed by handle; removal becomes O(1) and no reindex/leak exists. No defensible modern justification.

2. A full second copy of the factory in RAM with precomputed per-building screen-space caches. Modern practice is engine-state-as-truth (iterate the subsystems that already hold every transform) plus recompute trivially-derivable geometry at draw time from a per-CLASS table. Caching ~152-192B/building of recomputable corner/screen/rotation data is a dated RAM-for-FLOPs trade that loses at megabase scale.

3. FCanvas as the primary render-target rasterizer for frequent updates. Froyok benchmark: FCanvas recreates its entire draw setup every frame and is ~10x slower than the Slate/cached path. Modern primitives: GPU instancing (HISM/GPU Scene), SceneCapture of instanced geometry, or a cached RDG/compute pass. The global FCanvas::GetBatchedElements hook that reroutes EVERY canvas in the game (plus an unsafe cross-mod static_cast) is doubly dated, replaced entirely by the SceneCapture path.

4. Fixed 8192^2 RGBA8 render target with a full-screen opaque ClearItem every redraw. Modern: size the target to need (4096^2 or smaller / config), use a true scissored HW clear of only the dirty rect, persist and reuse the target, let GPU AA from instanced capture compensate for lower resolution. The full-surface software clear tile is pure wasted bandwidth.

5. Cancel-restart-the-coroutine-on-every-build-event redraw. Modern: debounced dirty-rect/dirty-cell accumulation with at most one budgeted redraw (or one CaptureSceneDeferred) per quiescence window; never discard completed draw work. Native orthographic tiling makes even the full-redraw case frame-bounded.

6. Synchronous per-join full-dataset serialize over a hand-rolled int16-sliced RCO with unchecked TMap::Find. Modern: a shared dirty-invalidated snapshot streamed via the ReliableMessaging plugin with a windowed pull and int32 counters.

NOT a fit despite being modern: Nanite (anti-pattern for flat 2D quads) and RVT for the live layer (poor with moving/changing meshes); both evaluated and scoped out.
netVerdict: Modern tooling makes this architecture decisively STRONGER and exposes NO new fatal availability gap; every load-bearing technique is usable from an SML mod on the UE 5.3.2 fork without engine-source changes. Decisive finds: (1) Satisfactory already instances its buildables via CSS AbstractInstance, so a per-class HISM marker layer plus orthographic SceneCapture works with the engine grain, not against it; (2) UE 5.3 SceneCaptureComponent2D has NATIVE orthographic tiling (bEnableOrthographicTiling, NumXTiles, NumYTiles) that splits one capture across N frames, a built-in zero-engine-source structural cure for the 2s TDR client crash (#14), the scariest failure; (3) global shaders plus RDG passes are confirmed registerable from a plugin (AddShaderSourceDirectoryMapping plus FSceneViewExtensionBase) as an advanced fallback. The one place modern tooling does NOT help and would mislead is RVT: the canonical in-game-map RVT author explicitly warns it struggles with moving/changing meshes, and a factory map is mutation-heavy by definition, so RVT is scoped to a static far-zoom pyramid only, not the live edit layer. Correct end-state: stable-handle slim data model (pure CPU, prerequisite, biggest ROI), then per-class HISM plus orthographic-tiled SceneCapture renderer (GPU-driven, TDR-proof, O(1) mutations), then ReliableMessaging windowed snapshot streaming for joins, with a chunked-FCanvas plus scissored-clear bridge to ship the TDR/VRAM fixes before the renderer rewrite clears art review. No depended-on technique is gated behind a newer engine version; the only availability caveats are fork-validation items (GetViewOwner isolation, persistent-target no-implicit-clear, shader module load phase in packaged builds), not blockers.

techniques.name: Per-class HISM + per-instance custom data (engine GPU Scene path)
techniques.whatItIs: One UHierarchicalInstancedStaticMeshComponent per buildable class on a hidden marker actor; each live buildable is one instance (a flat quad / unit box) with a GPU-resident FMatrix44f transform. Per-instance custom data floats (worldZ, layerId, categoryColorIndex) flow into an unlit material that clips by a MinZ/MaxZ scalar param and a layer mask. Add/remove buildable = AddInstance/RemoveInstance (O(1) amortized; HISM tail-swaps and renumbers exactly one instance). This is precisely the system Satisfactory itself uses (CSS AbstractInstance) for foundations/walls/belts, so the data is already instanced in-engine.
techniques.appliesTo: data model (replaces CurrentBuildingData second-copy), CPU per-event cost (O(1) vs O(N)), GPU redraw cost, RAM, Z-filter/layer-filter
techniques.benefit: Per-event ingestion O(N) to O(1); deletes the redirector, quadtree and Z-sort entirely. Per-building RAM ~344-432B to ~64B FMatrix44f (+12B custom data), much of it VRAM not system RAM. Z-filter/layer toggle become 2 scalar param writes plus one capture instead of O(N) array re-walk plus full redraw. Redraw cost moves to the GPU rasterizer (~O(visible instances)), independent of how many buildings changed.
techniques.caveats: Per-instance custom data is vertex-shader only; read it via a VertexInterpolator node to reach the pixel shader. Lightweight buildables have no stable AActor* identity; key by {class, lightweight-array-index} plus a generation counter or handles desync on engine-side renumber. The RemoveInstance tail-swap patch must be atomic with the one moved instance handle. Material-based Z/layer clip still pays vertex+raster work for hidden instances; toggle whole-component visibility for fully-disabled layers. Crisp 1px CPU lines are lost; belts/wires become thin oriented-box instances; needs art review.

techniques.name: USceneCaptureComponent2D orthographic capture with native Orthographic Tiling
techniques.whatItIs: An orthographic top-down USceneCaptureComponent2D (OrthoWidth = world width) captures the hidden instanced marker layer into the existing render target via CaptureSceneDeferred(), gated to ShowOnlyActorComponents(MarkerActor) using a GetViewOwner() override. UE 5.3 SceneCapture2D natively supports bEnableOrthographicTiling plus NumXTiles/NumYTiles, which splits one ortho capture across N frames, directly bounding GPU work per frame.
techniques.appliesTo: GPU redraw cost, the TDR client crash (#14), render-thread pacing, removing the FCanvas hook
techniques.benefit: Redraw becomes one debounced GPU capture instead of an O(N) game-thread FCanvas loop emitting ~9*N DrawItems in one unbounded RHI submission. Orthographic tiling structurally makes the 2s single-submission TDR impossible: a megabase capture is spread over NumXTiles*NumYTiles frames. LODDistanceFactor>1 further cuts capture cost. Eliminates the global FCanvas::GetBatchedElements hook (taxes every canvas in the game plus an unsafe cross-mod downcast).
techniques.caveats: Orthographic tiling REQUIRES CaptureSource = SceneColor; it is IGNORED (with a logged warning) for FinalColor sources, so a custom unlit/SceneColor pipeline is needed. Each capture is a real render-thread scene render: use bCaptureEveryFrame=false plus debounced dirty flag, coalescing same-frame events into <=1 capture/tick, or render-thread hitches/TDR return. GetViewOwner/ShowOnlyActorComponents isolation is version-fragile; verify hidden-flag resolution on the 5.3.2 fork. Dedicated server has no GPU: build no capture there.

techniques.name: Custom global shaders + RDG passes from a plugin (no engine source)
techniques.whatItIs: Register a plugin shader directory via AddShaderSourceDirectoryMapping in a PostConfigInit-phase module, declare shaders with IMPLEMENT_GLOBAL_SHADER/SHADER_USE_PARAMETER_STRUCT, and inject custom FRDGBuilder passes (AddPass / FPixelShaderUtils::AddFullscreenPass / compute) via an FSceneViewExtensionBase or around your own render-target draw. Enables a bespoke compute/raster rasterizer or scissored clear writing directly to the map RT.
techniques.appliesTo: GPU rasterization path (alternative to FCanvas and SceneCapture), scissored partial clears, compute-shader rasterization of rectangles/lines
techniques.benefit: Bypasses FCanvas entirely (Froyok: Canvas recreates draw setup every frame, ~10x slower than the cached path for RT updates). A custom RDG pass can do a true scissored HW clear of only the dirty rect (vs today 67M-texel full-screen opaque ClearItem) and batch all building primitives into one instanced draw or a compute rasterizer with explicit per-frame primitive budgeting.
techniques.caveats: Confirmed working without engine source on 4.27/5.0.3; the AddShaderSourceDirectoryMapping plus RDG AddPass API is stable through 5.3 but must be validated on CSS fork (SML packaged/shipping: confirm the shader module loads at PostConfigInit and .usf files ship). Scene-texture structs live in private engine headers, only an issue if reading scene textures, which a self-contained map RT pass does not need. Highest engineering complexity; only justified if neither HISM+SceneCapture nor chunked-FCanvas holds frame time.

techniques.name: Chunked / bounded FCanvas flush on a persistent render target
techniques.whatItIs: Keep the existing FCanvas to UCanvasRenderTarget2D path but, after a configurable MaxPrimitivesPerFrame (~20k), EndDrawCanvasToRenderTarget then co_await NextTick then re-Begin on the SAME persistent target WITHOUT re-clearing. Converts one unbounded RHI submission into ceil(primitives/budget) bounded submissions. Pair with a scissored clear sized to the already-computed dirty bounds and a persistent never-reallocated never-fully-cleared target.
techniques.appliesTo: the TDR crash (#14), GPU submission bounding, per-event clear bandwidth, lowest-risk path
techniques.benefit: Structurally eliminates the 2s single-submission TDR with a surgical change that keeps the entire current pipeline. Scissoring the clear turns a 67M-texel full-screen opaque clear into a few-hundred-texel clear for a single belt. Persistent-target reuse avoids per-redraw reallocation. Minimal-risk GPU fix shippable before any architectural rewrite.
techniques.caveats: The 2nd BeginDraw must preserve target contents (verify it does not implicitly clear on the 5.3.2 fork; the branch-history 'lines going crazy' note traces to exactly this). Still CPU-rasterized, so per-redraw game-thread cost remains O(drawn primitives); this bounds GPU cost and clear bandwidth, not CPU emit cost. FCanvas remains ~10x heavier than cached/instanced paths, so this is a bridge, not the end-state.

techniques.name: Slate SRetainerWidget (phase/frequency-throttled UI compositing)
techniques.whatItIs: Wrap the map widget in an SRetainerWidget/URetainerBox: it renders children to a render target once and composites that texture thereafter, with Phase/PhaseCount controlling refresh frequency (PhaseCount=2 means UI redraws at 30Hz in a 60Hz game). Materials can post-process the cached RT.
techniques.appliesTo: UI presentation layer (the Slate/UMG view that displays the RT), not the buildable rasterization itself
techniques.benefit: Decouples map-UI compositing cost from game frame rate; the heavy map texture is composited at a throttled phase instead of every frame, and pan/zoom material effects run on the cached RT for near-free. Complements (does not replace) fixing the underlying buildable redraw.
techniques.caveats: Retainer boxes allocate their own GPU render target (more VRAM) and add a compositing indirection; net win only if the wrapped subtree is genuinely expensive to re-tessellate each frame. It throttles UI presentation, not the buildable RT generation, so it does NOT address the #14 redraw/TDR root cause. Use Invalidation panels for the cheap static chrome around the map.

techniques.name: Uniform spatial hash grid over fixed world bounds (replaces TQuadTree int32 + redirector)
techniques.whatItIs: World bounds are compile-time constants, so replace the positional-index quadtree plus never-compacting IndexRedirector with a flat TArray of TArray of BuildingId (or TMap FIntPoint to TArray BuildingId) of ~50m cells keyed by STABLE handle. Add = insert id into overlapped cells O(1); remove = erase id O(1); dirty-rect query visits only overlapping cells. A TSparseArray slot is the stable id; a separate Z-index (sorted array or 1m Z-bands) carries the height filter.
techniques.appliesTo: THE central data-model flaw (root cause 1/2), per-event O(N) to O(1), the redirector memory/scan leak, initial-load O(N^2) to O(N)
techniques.benefit: Kills the O(N) reindex on every add/remove and the O(N^2) initial load; the per-event scan length becomes live count, never cumulative-lifetime placements (the session-long leak signature behind #14). Removes the 40B/building FBox2D the quadtree stored and the 4B/placement redirector tombstone. Decouples storage, spatial-culling and Z-filter, which were fatally conflated in one Z-sorted array.
techniques.caveats: Pure CPU data-structure change (no engine dependency); lowest risk, highest ROI, and a prerequisite for every rendering option above. Cell size must be tuned: too-small inflates per-building cell insertions for long belts/large foundations; too-large inflates dirty-rect query. TSparseArray slot reuse changes id-stability semantics; add a generation counter if the RCO/UI keys on id across remove+add. Dropping the Z-sort changes draw order; preserve overlap layering via the separate Z-index.

techniques.name: ReliableMessaging plugin for streamed, windowed dataset transfer to joining clients
techniques.whatItIs: Use the repo existing ReliableMessaging plugin (reliable large-payload messaging) to replace the hand-rolled RCO slice protocol: stream slices on demand from a single shared TSharedRef const TArray uint8 snapshot (regenerated on a dirty flag, pinned by all joiners), with a multi-MTU pull window and a widened (int32) slice counter.
techniques.appliesTo: network (dedicated-server join crash #9), per-join server RAM, join wall-clock
techniques.benefit: Shared snapshot makes join memory O(joiners*N) to O(N). Windowed pull (4-8 slices/ack) cuts a 200k-building join from ~2000 RTTs to a few hundred. Combined with the slim ~24-40B record (8-15x smaller payload) this is the scalable replacement for the synchronous per-join full serialize plus int16 overflow plus unchecked TMap::Find null-deref behind #9.
techniques.caveats: In-repo plugin; verify its API surface and that it handles backpressure/abort on mid-transfer disconnect (the exact #9 race). The shared snapshot must invalidate on every mutation and builds occurring DURING the pull must be replayed to the joiner, else stale/missing buildings. Keep transport reliable for correctness; do NOT adopt unreliable sequenced deltas yet (the resync state machine is the highest-risk networking piece and unnecessary for #9).

techniques.name: Runtime Virtual Texture tiled map pyramid
techniques.whatItIs: Author an RVT that materials write into via RuntimeVirtualTextureOutput; a SceneCapture samples the RVT through an ortho plane for the UI. RVT builds texel data on-demand on the GPU at the requested resolution, streaming only visible tiles, a tiled map pyramid with extreme texture-memory savings.
techniques.appliesTo: VRAM (alternative to the fixed 8192^2 256MB target), zoom LOD pyramid
techniques.benefit: On-demand tile residency instead of a permanent 256MB target; only visible/requested tiles and mips are resident, scaling memory with what is actually viewed rather than world size.
techniques.caveats: STRONG CAVEAT: the canonical in-game-map RVT author explicitly warns do not render moving meshes into an RVT; RVTs are tuned for STATIC geometry and struggle to keep up with frequent changes. A factory map is mutation-heavy (the entire problem), so RVT fights the workload. RVT also primarily targets landscape/material blending, adds CPU feedback overhead, and its dynamic-update story is weak. Treat as a VRAM-pyramid idea for the mostly-static far-zoom layer only, not the live edit layer. Lower priority than HISM+SceneCapture.

techniques.name: Async compute (RDG ERDGPassFlags::AsyncCompute) for the rasterization/clear pass
techniques.whatItIs: If a custom RDG rasterizer/clear pass is built, mark it ERDGPassFlags::AsyncCompute so map regeneration overlaps the main graphics queue on the async compute queue, with RHI transitions managing graphics-to-compute resource ownership.
techniques.appliesTo: GPU scheduling, overlap map regeneration with the main frame instead of serializing on the graphics queue
techniques.benefit: The off-screen map RT regeneration can run concurrently with the player main-view render, hiding its cost behind graphics-queue bubbles and reducing its frame-time contribution.
techniques.caveats: Only meaningful if the custom-RDG-shader path is adopted; not applicable to FCanvas or SceneCapture. Hardware/driver dependent (D3D12; gated by r.D3D12.AllowAsyncCompute / r.RDG.AsyncCompute and GPU support, AMD broadly, NVIDIA RTX3000+). Recent UE versions show async-compute GPU-crash reports; needs careful transition handling. A late-stage optimization, not a foundation.

techniques.name: Nanite for the 2D marker geometry
techniques.whatItIs: Using Nanite virtualized geometry for the flat quad/box marker meshes that represent buildables.
techniques.appliesTo: marker mesh rendering (evaluated and rejected)
techniques.benefit: None meaningful for this workload.
techniques.caveats: Explicitly NOT worth it: Nanite targets high-triangle-density / many-small-triangle meshes; flat low-poly quads add Nanite overhead with zero benefit, and over-triangulating flat surfaces is a known Nanite anti-pattern. Satisfactory on 5.3.2 also gates Nanite support per-platform. Use plain ISM/HISM instancing instead. Listed only to document it was considered and rejected.

target: Cartograph (Satisfactory factory-map mod) ground-up re-architecture — cross-cutting SOTA platform-capability research for the data model, spatial index, persistence, rendering, and join-time replication. NOTE: the actual engine is CSS-forked Unreal Engine 5.6.1 (FactoryGame.uproject EngineAssociation="5.6.1-CSS"), SML ^3.12.0, Satisfactory 1.2 (GameVersion >=491125) — NOT UE 5.3.2 as the prompt assumed. This materially widens the available-technique set; every availability tag below is assessed against UE 5.6.1-CSS + SML 3.12, usable from a GameFeature mod without engine source changes.

techniques.name: AbstractInstance / AAbstractInstanceManager stable-handle instanced rendering (in-repo plugin)
techniques.whatItIs: Satisfactory's own instanced-mesh system, vendored at Plugins/AbstractInstance. SetInstanceFromDataStatic(owner, transform, FInstanceData, OutHandle, bInitializeHidden) adds one instance to a per-mesh ULightweightHierarchicalInstancedStaticMeshComponent and returns an FInstanceOwnerHandlePtr (a STABLE handle, not a positional index). RemoveInstance(handle) does a RemoveSwap and internally patches the one moved instance's handle, so add/remove are O(1) amortized with no reindex and no tombstone leak. FInstanceData exposes NumCustomDataFloats (up to 20 per docs) consumed via SetCustomPrimitiveDataOnHandle(handle, floats) -> per-instance custom data readable in the material shader. MaxMeshInstancePerComponent buckets instances; MarkDirtyDeferred coalesces render-state updates to end-of-frame. ResolveHit/ResolveOverlap give spatial point/area queries.
techniques.appliesTo: data model (replaces CurrentBuildingData + redirector + quadtree with the GPU instance buffer as the single render copy), spatial index (ResolveHit/ResolveOverlap), rendering (marker layer for a SceneCapture or HUD-composited layer), CPU/RAM, VRAM
techniques.benefit: Cures root causes 1 & 2: stable handle => no O(N) BuildingDataIndexRedirector reindex per add/remove, no never-compacting tombstone leak, O(1) ingestion instead of O(N) (kills #14 lag spikes and the O(N^2) load). The instance transform buffer (FMatrix44f, 64 B GPU-resident) becomes the only render-side copy, so the ~344-432 B/building second-copy FBuildingData store can be deleted on the host. Per-instance custom data (worldZ, layerId, categoryColor) moves Z-filter and layer toggles to material clip(), eliminating the Z-sort coupling that forced unstable array positions. RemoveSwap patches exactly one handle vs. the current O(N) redirector walk.
techniques.caveats: fg-sml-specific because it is the FG/CSS plugin, but it ships in this repo (Plugins/AbstractInstance) and is a commented-out dep in Cartograph.Build.cs, so enabling it is a one-line change — no engine edit. ULightweightHierarchicalInstancedStaticMeshComponent currently derives from UInstancedStaticMeshComponent (not HISM) in this repo's copy — per-instance culling but no HLOD clustering, fine for a flat map. Lightweight buildables have no AActor* identity, so the key must be {class, lightweight-index} with a generation guard; the engine can renumber lightweight indices. NumCustomDataFloats raises per-instance buffer size. ResolveHit/Overlap are physics-trace based, not a free range query over the whole set.

techniques.name: ReliableMessaging bulk-data transport (in-repo plugin) for join-time dataset streaming
techniques.whatItIs: A complete reliable, chunked, ack-windowed, tagged large-payload messaging stack at Plugins/ReliableMessaging. UReliableMessagingSubsystem::SendTaggedMessage(Player, FGameplayTag, TArray<uint8>) streams an arbitrarily large payload as MessageHeader + N ChunkHeader packets each sized to (MaxPacketSize - header), with an Ack opcode the receiver returns (cumulative: ack of chunk n implies all prior). MessageIdType is uint64 (no int16 overflow), the reader reassembles incrementally and fires HandleMessageReceived only on completion, and FullySentMessages are retained for resend-on-reconnect. Transport backends exist for TCP, Steam P2P, and EOS P2P; registers via UNetDriver and a per-PlayerController component.
techniques.appliesTo: network (join-time transfer of the derived building dataset to clients that lack subsystem data), replication, RAM (streaming vs. materializing the whole buffer)
techniques.benefit: Correct replacement for Cartograph's hand-rolled RCO slice protocol that causes root cause 5 (the #9 server crash): removes the int16 slice-count overflow (uint64 ids, SizeType lengths), the unchecked TMap::Find null-deref racing a 10s timeout (lifecycle owned by the subsystem/connection, not an ad-hoc per-player FBufferWriter map), the reliable-multicast flood, and the move-unsafe FBufferWriter. Chunking is MTU-aware and ack-windowed, so a 200k-building join becomes a few hundred bounded round-trips with incremental reassembly instead of one synchronous full serialize. Reuses a battle-tested CSS transport.
techniques.caveats: Ships in this repo's Plugins/ (Copyright Epic/CSS). It moves bytes only — Cartograph must define the wire schema (quantized slim record) and a snapshot-versioning/dirty-replay scheme so builds during a transfer aren't missed. Requires a registered FGameplayTag channel. Backend selection (TCP vs Steam/EOS P2P) depends on the session net driver; confirm the dedicated-server path uses an available transport. Server still needs a single shared TSharedRef snapshot (regenerated on dirty) pinned across joiners to keep join memory O(N) not O(joiners*N).

techniques.name: USceneCaptureComponent2D orthographic capture with show-only isolation (GPU rasterization of the map)
techniques.whatItIs: A top-down orthographic USceneCaptureComponent2D renders a hidden per-class instanced marker layer into the existing UCanvasRenderTarget2D in one GPU pass. Isolation via PrimitiveRenderMode=UseShowOnlyList + ShowOnlyActors/ShowOnlyActorComponents(MarkerActor), plus a GetViewOwner() override so per-owner bOnlyOwnerSee filtering resolves to the marker layer and never the real world. bCaptureEveryFrame=false + CaptureSceneDeferred() makes redraw an explicit, debounced, fixed-cost capture. UE supports orthographic tiling (render in TileCount frames) when CaptureSource uses SceneColor — a native way to bound per-frame GPU cost.
techniques.appliesTo: rendering (replaces the CPU FCanvas rasterizer, the global FCanvas::GetBatchedElements hook, and the scissor render item), GPU/VRAM, CPU (game thread no longer rasterizes)
techniques.benefit: Structurally eliminates root causes 3 & 4: redraw cost moves off the game thread to one GPU capture whose cost is ~O(visible instances) regardless of how many buildings changed, so a belt drag is instance-buffer mutations + one deferred capture (no cancel/restart thrash, no per-primitive co_await, no 0.5-1M-primitive single RHI submission). Deletes the process-wide FCanvas hook (a cross-mod hazard + per-batch tax on every UI canvas). GPU MSAA gives cleaner lines than 1px-per-cm CPU draws, permitting a smaller render target. Orthographic tiling natively chunks the capture to dodge the ~2s Windows TDR.
techniques.caveats: GetViewOwner()/ShowOnlyActorComponents isolation is version-fragile and must be re-verified on UE 5.6.1-CSS (the Cartograph_2.0 POC used exactly this but never compiled). A full ortho capture of a megabase can hitch unless debounced (bCaptureEveryFrame=false, <=1 capture/frame, only when the map UI is open). Orthographic tiling requires CaptureSource=SceneColor (not FinalColorLDR), changing the color/material path. Dedicated servers have no GPU: capture and marker actor must be client-only; server keeps only the authoritative replication snapshot. Icon buildings must become a material/texture-array path (no FCanvas TSoftObjectPtr blit); pin icon textures. Full rendering rewrite — gate on art review.

techniques.name: RDG/RHI scissored ClearRenderTargetView + bounded chunked EndDraw flush (keep the canvas path)
techniques.whatItIs: Within the existing BeginDrawCanvasToRenderTarget path: (a) replace the full-screen opaque FCanvasTileItem clear with a true hardware ClearRenderTargetView restricted to the already-computed scissor bounds (a near-free HW clear vs. a 67M-texel rasterized quad); (b) after a config MaxPrimitivesPerFrame, EndDrawCanvasToRenderTarget -> co_await NextTick -> re-BeginDraw the same persistent target WITHOUT re-clearing, converting one unbounded RHI submission into ceil(primitives/budget) bounded submissions. UE's tiled-render model (per-tile command buffers submitted separately) is the engine's own documented TDR-avoidance pattern.
techniques.appliesTo: rendering, GPU (TDR avoidance), VRAM bandwidth
techniques.benefit: Lowest-risk structural fix for the TDR (root cause 3) that keeps the FCanvas architecture: bounds every GPU submission so a megabase full redraw drains over many frames instead of exceeding the ~2s driver timeout. The scissored HW clear turns the per-event full-screen 256 MB opaque clear into a few-hundred-texel clear sized to the dirty rect, cutting per-event bandwidth by orders of magnitude. No data-model or wire change required; complements the stable-handle store rather than depending on the SceneCapture rewrite.
techniques.caveats: The 2nd BeginDraw must preserve target contents (verify it does not implicitly clear on UE 5.6.1); a cancel mid-chunk leaves a partial map that self-heals on next completion. ClearRenderTargetView under a scissor must run on the render thread via an RDG/RHI AddPass lambda (avoid FRHICommandListImmediate so the pass stays parallelizable). The existing custom FCartographCanvasRenderItem already sets a scissor rect, so the plumbing largely exists. Canvas-to-RT is ~10x slower than Slate for the same work, so this is a bridge, not the end state — pairs with reducing RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE (256 MB->64 MB at 4096).

techniques.name: Engine-as-truth iteration of AFGBuildableSubsystem / AFGLightweightBuildableSubsystem (drop the second copy)
techniques.whatItIs: Read buildables directly from the engine's authoritative stores instead of maintaining a parallel array. AFGLightweightBuildableSubsystem::mBuildableClassToInstanceArray (TMap<TSubclassOf<AFGBuildable>, TArray<FRuntimeBuildableInstanceData>>) holds belts/pipes/foundations/walls as lightweight instances (no per-instance actor); AFGBuildableSubsystem::GetAllBuildablesRef() holds heavy actors. On a host both are already in RAM (Cartograph's gather reads them at module.cpp:383-388, but by value). Pass them by const-ref and iterate per dirty region at draw time; keep only a spatial index + Z-index keyed by stable handle.
techniques.appliesTo: data model (eliminates the host-side second factory copy), RAM, CPU (no by-value deep copy at load)
techniques.benefit: Cures root cause 2 on the host outright: the ~360-430 MB @1M-building duplicate FBuildingData store + ~152-192 B/building precomputed draw caches become recompute-on-draw from the engine arrays, so host resident memory for the dataset approaches zero (only the spatial index + per-class draw table + Z-index remain). Passing mBuildableClassToInstanceArray by const-ref instead of by value (the current 'Intentional copies') removes the O(N) deep-copy load spike that transiently doubles the factory in RAM. Only dedicated-server CLIENTS (which lack the subsystem data) need a slim replicated store.
techniques.caveats: FGLightweightBuildableSubsystem internals (mBuildableClassToInstanceArray, FRuntimeBuildableInstanceData layout) are not in public web docs — confirm field names/visibility against the SML/FactoryGame headers in this engine fork (Cartograph already references them, so they are reachable, possibly via AccessTransformers/friend). Lightweight indices can be renumbered by the engine on its own removals, so a generation-guarded {class,index} key is required. World Partition means not every buildable is loaded/resident at all times on the client; the design must tolerate streamed-out regions. SML's official position: World Partition itself is not yet moddable, so you cannot drive server-side region streaming, only read what is loaded.

techniques.name: IFGSaveInterface-persisted derived dataset (server-side, skip re-gather on load)
techniques.whatItIs: Persist Cartograph's derived spatial index / slim record set in the save via IFGSaveInterface on a mod subsystem: override ShouldSave()->true, mark the serialized fields with the SaveGame UPROPERTY flag, and use PreSaveGame/PostLoadGame hooks to (re)build runtime structures. Per-player/non-buildable data persists via Actor Mixins / SCS hooks attaching a component to PlayerState. FGBuildable already implements IFGSaveInterface (but ShouldSave defaults false).
techniques.appliesTo: persistence (avoid O(N^2)/O(N log N) full re-gather on every load), RAM at load, CPU at load
techniques.benefit: Lets the host persist the already-built spatial index + Z-index + per-class table so a world load does not re-run the full InitialBuildableGather (today O(N^2) due to the redirector and a by-value engine-map copy). Combined with the stable-handle store, load becomes deserialize-then-validate rather than rebuild-from-scratch, removing the multi-second-to-minute load hang (root cause 1's load-time manifestation). Server-side persistence of a slim snapshot also accelerates dedicated-server client joins.
techniques.caveats: Only SaveGame-flagged UPROPERTYs serialize; raw TSparseArray/std::variant POD must be wrapped or custom-serialized. Avoid the SkipSerialization flag and circular GatherDependencies. The persisted derived data can drift from the live factory if other mods/the engine mutate buildables outside Cartograph's hooks, so PostLoadGame must reconcile against the live subsystem arrays (treat the save as a cache, not the source of truth). Versioning required so a format change doesn't corrupt old saves. Optional optimization, not a correctness fix.

techniques.name: UE5Coro frame-budgeted coroutines with debounced dirty-rect convergence (already vendored)
techniques.whatItIs: UE5Coro is vendored in the mod (Source/Cartograph/Public/UE5Coro, incl. FTickTimeBudget). End-state pattern: drain PendingAdd/Remove into the (now O(1)) spatial structures continuously, accumulate a TSet<FIntPoint> DirtyCells / dirty-rect, and run at most ONE budgeted redraw per quiescence window — never Cancel()+restart the in-flight coroutine on every build event, and never discard completed draw work. Await once per building/batch, not per primitive.
techniques.appliesTo: rendering convergence, CPU (game-thread frame pacing), amplifier root cause 4
techniques.benefit: Eliminates the cancel-restart thrash (root cause 4): under a belt drag the map converges incrementally instead of producing zero completed frames until the player stops. Awaiting once per building instead of ~9x per primitive removes millions of FPlatformTime::Cycles() awaiter calls per megabase redraw. Coalescing many same-frame events into one capped redraw is the correct expression of issue #10's frame-relative budget, and composes with either the chunked-canvas or SceneCapture renderer.
techniques.caveats: UE5Coro is bundled in-repo (no external dep), already used by the current RedrawMapCoroutine, so this is a control-flow refactor not a new dependency. Pre-resolve/pin icon textures before opening the canvas so the loop never co_awaits AsyncLoadObject mid-pass (current bug). DirtyCells accumulation must survive cancellation correctly (the partial_redraw branch lost the dirty rect across cancel/restart — a known regression to design around). On dedicated server, skip the draw-oriented bookkeeping entirely.

techniques.name: Uniform spatial hash grid over fixed world bounds (replace TQuadTree<int32>+redirector)
techniques.whatItIs: World bounds are compile-time constants (WEST/EAST/NORTH/SOUTH_BOUND, ~7.5km). Replace TQuadTree<int32> + BuildingDataIndexRedirector with TMap<FIntPoint,TArray<BuildingId>> (or a flat TArray<TArray<BuildingId>> over GRID_W*GRID_H cells, ~50m cells -> ~150x150). Insert a stable BuildingId into each overlapped cell on add (O(cells)), erase on remove (O(cells)), query a dirty rect by visiting overlapping cells only. Z-filter lives on a separate sorted Z-index or 1m Z-bands so the master store needs no ordering.
techniques.appliesTo: spatial index, data model (decouples storage / spatial culling / Z-filter), CPU, RAM
techniques.benefit: Minimal-rewrite cure for root cause 1 if AbstractInstance is not adopted: O(1) insert/erase keyed by stable handle, no positional renumbering, no redirector, no tombstone leak, no 40 B/building FBox2D quadtree element, no node-split retention. Cache-friendly and bounded by world size (~22500 cells) not by building count. Decoupling the Z-filter onto its own index removes the operator<=> Z-sort coupling that was the single decision forcing unstable array positions.
techniques.caveats: Pure-code, no engine/plugin dependency — fully portable. Cell size is a tuning tradeoff: too small inflates per-building cell-list insertions for long belts/large foundations; too large inflates dirty-rect query cost. Large multi-cell buildings store a small cell list per record (or recompute on remove). If the SceneCapture/AbstractInstance path is adopted, GPU frustum culling on the capture subsumes most of this and the grid is needed only for interaction/picking and dirty-rect bookkeeping.

techniques.name: Single-precision FVector3f + quantized slim record / NetSerialize
techniques.whatItIs: Shrink the resident/wire record to {uint32 ClassHash; FVector3f Position (12 B); float YawRadians; EBuildingDataType:8; uint16 ExtraIndex} ~24-28 B, with spline/wire/beam payloads in side-tables indexed by ExtraIndex. Drop the full FTransform (quat+scale 96 B) — scale is irrelevant to a top-down map and yaw is the only rotation drawn. NetSerialize already proves this minimal record: it sends classHash + quantized position + compressed yaw and deliberately drops scale and the caches.
techniques.appliesTo: data model, RAM, network bandwidth, VRAM (smaller per-instance custom data)
techniques.benefit: 8-15x record shrink (~344-432 B -> ~24-28 B): 1M buildings ~360-430 MB -> ~26 MB resident on dedicated-server clients; proportionally smaller join payloads over ReliableMessaging. Single-precision position has ~0.05 cm worst-case error at the 7.5km map edge — visually irrelevant at 4096/8192 px. Variant-driven over-allocation (every spline paying ~160-216 B for an FNormalDataCache it never uses) is eliminated by moving extras to typed side-tables.
techniques.caveats: Pure-code. Must remove any exact-equality position compares (the old operator== did FTransform.Equals) since identity is now the stable handle, not the value. Recomputing ScreenPosition/Corners/Size/Rotation at draw time must reproduce the old FillInCache math pixel-identically — extract a shared pure helper used both ways during transition, verify on a large save, then delete the stored fields. Per-class lookups (size override, category, layer) must move to a TMap<uint32,FClassDrawInfo> built once (bounded by ~hundreds of classes), not stored per building.

techniques.name: Iris next-gen replication (UE 5.6) — evaluated and NOT recommended for this mod
techniques.whatItIs: Iris is UE's opt-in next-gen networking system (still Experimental in 5.6/5.7), enabled via bUseIris in *.Target.cs + net.Iris.UseIrisReplication=1 + the Iris plugin, designed for hundreds of concurrent replicated actors with custom NetSerialize fragments.
techniques.appliesTo: network/replication (considered as an alternative to the RCO + ReliableMessaging path)
techniques.benefit: In principle, more scalable delta replication for large replicated object counts; break-even around ~100 concurrent replicated actors.
techniques.caveats: Enabling Iris is a PROJECT/Target.cs-level toggle that changes the whole game's replication path — not something a single GameFeature mod can or should flip on CSS's shipped FactoryGame build without engine/target control, and it would conflict with the base game's replication. Cartograph's join-time problem is a one-shot bulk transfer, not high-frequency many-actor replication, so Iris is the wrong tool: ReliableMessaging already solves the bulk-streaming need from inside the mod. Listed to explicitly rule it out and steer the design to ReliableMessaging.

modernizationRecommendations:
Anchor the redesign on three in-repo CSS primitives, all usable from the GameFeature mod against UE 5.6.1-CSS without engine edits, and stage them so each is independently shippable.

1) DATA MODEL + SPATIAL INDEX (cures root causes 1, 2, the leak, the O(N^2) load): Make identity a STABLE HANDLE, never an array position. Two viable end-states that converge on the same record: (a) keep the canvas renderer and use TSparseArray<FSlimBuildingRecord> + a uniform hash grid over the fixed world bounds + a separate Z-index + a per-class FClassDrawInfo table; or (b) go GPU-resident and let AbstractInstance's per-class instanced components BE the store (the FInstanceOwnerHandlePtr is the stable handle; the FMatrix44f instance buffer is the only render copy). Either way: delete BuildingDataIndexRedirector and TQuadTree<int32>, drop the precomputed FNormalDataCache/FRectangleDataCache/VisualBoxCache (recompute on draw / push to per-instance custom data), shrink the record to ~24-28 B, pass the engine arrays by const-ref, and on the HOST iterate AFGBuildableSubsystem/AFGLightweightBuildableSubsystem as truth so the second copy disappears entirely. Move the Z-filter and layer toggles to per-instance custom data + material clip() (AbstractInstance gives up to 20 floats/instance) so storage needs no ordering.

2) RENDERING (cures root causes 3, 4): Two tiers. Tier-1 (low risk, keeps canvas): scissored hardware ClearRenderTargetView + chunked bounded EndDraw/NextTick flush + RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE 8192->4096 (256->64 MB VRAM) + debounced one-redraw-per-quiescence convergence via the already-vendored UE5Coro FTickTimeBudget, awaiting once per building not per primitive. Tier-2 (end state, bigger): a hidden per-class AbstractInstance marker layer captured by an orthographic USceneCaptureComponent2D (bCaptureEveryFrame=false + CaptureSceneDeferred, GetViewOwner/ShowOnlyActorComponents isolation), which deletes the process-wide FCanvas::GetBatchedElements hook and makes redraw fixed-cost on the GPU. Use orthographic tiling and/or the chunked-flush budget to keep any single submission under the ~2s TDR.

3) JOIN-TIME REPLICATION (cures root cause 5, #9): Replace the hand-rolled RCO slice protocol with ReliableMessaging's SendTaggedMessage bulk transport (uint64 message ids, MTU-aware chunking, cumulative acks, incremental reassembly, resend-on-reconnect). Server holds ONE shared TSharedRef snapshot of the slim quantized records, regenerated on a dirty flag and pinned across all joiners (join memory O(N) not O(joiners*N)); replay builds that occur during a transfer. Optionally persist the host's derived index via IFGSaveInterface (treat as a cache reconciled against the live subsystem in PostLoadGame) to skip the full re-gather on world load.

Recommended sequencing: Phase A = stable-handle store + grid + slim record + const-ref gather + drop derived caches (cures #14 lag/leak/load and most of the memory complaint, low-medium risk, no renderer change). Phase B = Tier-1 render fixes (scissored clear, 4096 target, chunked flush, debounced convergence) — cures the TDR cheaply. Phase C = ReliableMessaging join transport + shared snapshot — cures #9. Phase D (optional end state) = AbstractInstance + SceneCapture renderer, gated on art review and GetViewOwner isolation verification on 5.6.1-CSS.
deprecatedApproaches:
Patterns in the current architecture that a modern UE 5.6.1-CSS primitive now supersedes:

- POSITIONAL-INDEX SPATIAL INDEX + INDEX REDIRECTOR: Storing array positions in TQuadTree<int32> and patching them with a never-compacting BuildingDataIndexRedirector is the central anti-pattern. Superseded by stable handles — either AbstractInstance's FInstanceOwnerHandlePtr (RemoveSwap patches one handle) or a TSparseArray slot id. The redirector should not exist.

- SECOND IN-RAM COPY OF THE FACTORY: A parallel TArray<FBuildingData> duplicating AFGBuildableSubsystem/AFGLightweightBuildableSubsystem is dead weight on the host. The engine arrays are the source of truth; the GPU instance buffer is the render copy. Only dedicated-server clients (no subsystem data) need a slim store.

- PRECOMPUTED PER-BUILDING SCREEN-SPACE CACHES: FNormalDataCache/FRectangleDataCache/VisualBoxCache store ~152-192 B/building of data that is a pure function of Transform + per-class info (and the corner math is computed twice). Recompute on draw from a per-class table, or push worldZ/layer/color into per-instance custom data.

- PROCESS-WIDE FCanvas::GetBatchedElements HOOK: Rerouting every canvas in the game through the mod's render item (with an unchecked static_cast of an arbitrary render batch) to apply a scissor to ONE target is a cross-mod hazard and a per-frame tax. Superseded by either a dedicated RDG/RHI scissor pass around the mod's own EndDraw, or by dropping FCanvas entirely for a SceneCapture.

- FULL-SCREEN OPAQUE CLEAR TILE PER REDRAW: A 67M-texel rasterized quad as a 'clear' is superseded by a hardware ClearRenderTargetView under a scissor (or the capture clearing its own target once).

- FIXED 8192x8192 RGBA8 TARGET: 256 MB of permanent VRAM at ~1.09 cm/px is far finer than a minimap needs; 4096 (64 MB) plus GPU AA is the modern default, ideally config-exposed.

- HAND-ROLLED RCO SLICE PROTOCOL with int16 counters, unchecked TMap::Find, synchronous full serialize, reliable NetMulticast per build event, and a move-unsafe FBufferWriter: entirely superseded by the ReliableMessaging plugin's chunked/ack-windowed/uint64 transport.

- CANCEL-RESTART REDRAW COROUTINE: Cancelling the in-flight redraw on every build event (never converging mid-drag) is superseded by debounced dirty-rect accumulation with at most one budgeted redraw per quiescence window using the already-vendored UE5Coro FTickTimeBudget.

NOTE on the prompt premise: the stated 'UE 5.3.2' is outdated for this repo — FactoryGame.uproject targets 5.6.1-CSS and SML ^3.12.0, so 5.5/5.6-era techniques (Iris existence, render-thread parallelization, current AbstractInstance/ISM custom-data, UE5Coro) are in scope. The one genuinely-newer/unsuitable item is Iris (project-level, not mod-flippable; wrong tool for a one-shot bulk transfer).
netVerdict: Modern tooling makes this architecture decisively STRONGER and exposes no fatal availability gap — every cure for the five verified root causes is reachable from a GameFeature mod on UE 5.6.1-CSS + SML 3.12 WITHOUT engine source changes, and the three highest-leverage primitives (AbstractInstance, ReliableMessaging, UE5Coro) already ship inside this very repo. The redesign is not a research bet: stable-handle storage (AbstractInstance handle or TSparseArray) collapses root causes 1, 2, the leak, and the O(N^2) load simultaneously; ReliableMessaging's chunked ack-windowed transport replaces the crash-prone RCO (#9) wholesale; a scissored HW clear + chunked flush (or a SceneCapture) structurally bounds GPU work under the TDR threshold; and engine-as-truth iteration deletes the host-side second copy outright. The single most consequential research finding is a CORRECTION: the engine is 5.6.1-CSS, not 5.3.2, which only widens the toolset — nothing the design needs requires a newer engine than what is shipped. The one real platform LIMIT to design around is that World Partition is not yet moddable, so the architecture must treat streamed-out regions and lightweight-index renumbering as expected (generation-guarded keys, reconcile-on-load) rather than assume the whole factory is always resident. With that constraint respected, modern tooling turns a quadratic, leaking, TDR-prone, crash-on-join design into an O(1)-ingestion, flat-memory, GPU-bounded, reliably-streamed one.
